# skogai <module> <cmd>...: run a module's argc command with its env (`skogai module env`);
# anything else goes to core

export SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH="${SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH:+$SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH:}$root/modules"
core="$root/modules/core/argc.sh"

case "${1:-}" in
"" | -* | config | module | help) ;;
*)
    if cmd="$(argc --argc-run "$core" module command "$1" 2>/dev/null)"; then
        eval "$(argc --argc-run "$core" module env "$1")"
        shift
        exec argc --argc-run "$cmd" "$@"
    fi
    ;;
esac

# skogai modules

a module is one thing skogai can do, packaged so it can be found, run,
configured and copied into a repo as a unit. the argc script is one part of
it; the files it works with and its config defaults are the rest.

`skogai module check` enforces what this spec says a module must be.
`modules/core` and `modules/memory` are the reference modules.

## layout

```
<name>/
  module.md        required: manifest (frontmatter) and what it is (body)
  argc.sh          optional: the command, named by `command:`
  templates/ ...   optional: anything it offers, named by `files:`
  tests/*.bats     its own tests; not offered unless listed in `files:`
  tests/fixtures/  examples its schemas are held to (with `type`)
  module.local.md  local overrides, never shipped
```

the directory name is the module name.

## module.md

```markdown
---
type: module
name: memory
description: one fact per file, each with a stale_after; expired ones get decided on
command: argc.sh
tools: [yq]
requires: [core]
files:
  - templates/
config:
  dir: memory
  stale-days: 30
---

# memory

what it is, when to use it, what each config key means.
```

| field | | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | required | `module` | |
| `name` | required | string | lowercase, one segment (`^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$`), same as the directory |
| `description` | required | string | one line, what it is; shown by `module ls` |
| `command` | optional | path | its argc script, relative to the module dir; `skogai <name>` runs it |
| `tools` | optional | list | executables it needs on `PATH` |
| `requires` | optional | list | modules it needs; every module but `core` requires `core` |
| `files` | optional | list | paths it offers beyond `module.md` and `command`; a path ending in `/` is a whole directory |
| `config` | optional | map | config defaults, read as `<name>.<key>` |

a module consists of exactly `module.md`, `command` and `files`. nothing else
is copied on install; anything else in the directory is the source's own.

the body is prose for humans and agents: what the module is, every config key
and what it means, and anything a user decides when installing it.

## names

- `core`, `config`, `module` and `help` are reserved: `skogai config ...` is
  always core.
- config keys are lowercase; `.` is a relation and `-` is part of a name, so
  `memory.stale-days` is `SKOGAI_MEMORY_STALEDAYS` as env.

## where modules are found

in this order, the first module by a name wins:

| layer | where |
|---|---|
| `local` | `.skogai/modules/` at the git root (or `$SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR/modules`) |
| `global` | `~/.config/skogai/modules/` (or `$SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR/modules`) |
| `source` | each dir on `$SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH`, by default the plugin's `modules/` |

a module runs from wherever it is found; installing is not needed to use it.
an installed copy shadows its source, a local one shadows a global one.

## installing

installing copies a module into `local` or `global` so it can be edited there.
it is an offer, never a takeover:

- `skogai module add <name|path>` prints the plan, one line per file: `add`
  (missing, will copy), `same`, or `keep` (there and different, never
  overwritten). it exits `1` if anything would be added.
- `--apply` copies. `--to local|global` picks the layer, default
  `core.module.install`.
- `skogai module diff <name>` shows how an installed copy differs from its source.
- nothing outside `.skogai/` (local) or `~/.config/skogai/` (global) is written.

## config

a module's keys live under its name. the layers, later wins:

1. `config:` in every found `module.md` (defaults)
2. system, global, local: git-config files `config` in `/etc/skogai`,
   `~/.config/skogai`, `.skogai`
3. `config:` in each module's `module.local.md`
4. `--file` layers (`skogai config` only)
5. `SKOGAI_*` env

`skogai config set --module <name> <name>.<key> <value>` writes a module's
`module.local.md`: beside an installed copy's `module.md`, and for a source
module in `.skogai/modules/<name>/`, never into the source.
`skogai config get <key> --show-origin` says which layer won.

## skogai

`skogai` is the runner; argc is the engine under it.

- in Claude Code sessions it is this plugin's `bin/skogai`, on the Bash tool's
  `PATH` while the plugin is enabled. it finds modules when it runs, so
  nothing needs registering. its `SessionStart` hook runs
  `skogai module build --to global` and puts the built `skogai` first on
  the Bash tool's `PATH` (via `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`), so `skogai --help` lists
  every module found from where the session started.
- in a shell, `skogai module build` generates a static `skogai`: one argc
  file with a forwarding recipe for core's groups and every module found
  from there, so `--help`, completion and man pages cover all of them. every
  run still goes through the `bin/skogai` that built it, and a module found
  after the build runs too, only without help and completion. the build is
  throwaway, in `.skogai/tmp/skogai/` (or the global dir's): `bin/`,
  `man/man1/`, `completions/skogai.sh` for `ARGC_COMPLETIONS_PATH`, and
  `completions/skogai.{bash,zsh,fish}`. it prints the env lines for
  `PATH`, `MANPATH` and `ARGC_COMPLETIONS_PATH`; putting them in a shell, a
  `.envrc` or mise is up to the user. the first build runs the checkout's
  `bin/skogai` by path.
- `skogai module sandbox [dir]` (default `$TMPDIR/skogai`) is an empty
  skogai to try things in: `system/` and `global/` layers, a git repo
  `repo/` with every module found from here installed in its `.skogai/modules`
  (from its source when it has one) and `skogai` built there. it prints the
  env lines that switch a shell into it (`eval "$(skogai module sandbox)"`,
  fish `skogai module sandbox | source`): no `SKOGAI_*` config from outside,
  the three layer dirs, the built `skogai` on `PATH`, `cd repo`. it also
  writes `<dir>/run`, the same switch for one command (`/tmp/skogai/run
  skogai memory ls`, a shell with none), for callers whose env does not
  persist between commands, like an agent's Bash tool. rerunning replaces
  it; a dir it did not make is refused.

## the command

an argc script. `skogai <name> <args>` runs it with `argc --argc-run` from the
caller's directory, with this env (`skogai module env <name>`):

| var | |
|---|---|
| `SKOGAI_MODULE` | its name |
| `SKOGAI_MODULE_DIR` | its directory, wherever it was found; its `files:` are here |
| `SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR` | the local `.skogai`, absolute |
| `SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR` | the global dir, absolute |
| `SKOGAI_<NAME>_<KEY>` | each of its own resolved config keys |

rules:

- read paths and config from that env, never from `$PWD` or its own location.
  start with `: "${SKOGAI_MODULE_DIR:?run me as \`skogai <name>\`}"`.
- `# @meta binname skogai <name>` so help and man pages read right;
  `# @meta require-tools` matches `tools:`.
- a positional `~` argument takes everything after it, flags included: put
  options before it.
- exit `0` ok, `1` a finding or an unapplied change (like `diff`), `2` usage.
- pure by default: a recipe that changes an existing file takes `--apply` and
  without it prints what it would do. creating a new file is fine; overwriting
  one is refused.
- don't name a recipe after a bash builtin (`eval`, `cd`, `exec`, `set`); argc's
  generated code calls them. group them instead (`config::set`).
- other modules are called as `skogai <other> ...`, never by path.

## tests

bats. `skogai module test [name]...` runs, for each module:

1. the contract, core's `tests/contract.bats`: `module check` has no errors,
   `--help` exits 0, the command refuses to run outside `skogai` and says so, every
   `config:` default resolves under its name, `module env` is right, `add` is
   a plan and `--apply` installs, and the installed copy passes check and runs.
   then `tests/contract.bats` of each module in `requires` (not transitive)
   that has one, with `SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE` still the module under test.
2. its own `tests/*.bats`, from its source when it has one; its own
   `tests/contract.bats` is what it holds others to, not run against itself.

a module that requires `type` ships fixtures for each `schema/<x>.json` it
offers: `tests/fixtures/<x>/valid/*` and `tests/fixtures/<x>/invalid/*`, both
non-empty, in its source only (not in `files:`). type's contract checks every
valid one passes and every invalid one fails, the way `skogai type check`
checks instances (`skogai type check --schema <module>.<x> <file>...`).

a test file starts with `load "$SKOGAI_TEST_HELPER"` (core's
`tests/helper.bash`). every test then runs in an empty git repo
(`$REPO`, with `$LOCAL` its `.skogai`) with its own system and global layers
and no `SKOGAI_*` config from the caller, so nothing outside
`BATS_TEST_TMPDIR` is touched. the module under test is a source there.
helpers: `skogai`, `module_dir`, `module_field`, `assert_status`,
`assert_output_has`, `refute_output_has`, `assert_file`. a file with its own
`setup()` calls `skogai_setup` first.

set state the way a user would (`skogai config set`, `skogai module add`),
not by writing layer files.

a bare `! cmd` never fails a bats test: end a helper function with it, or
use `[[ ... ]]`. test the failure paths too: what a command refuses, and
that a failure leaves nothing behind.

## creating one

1. `skogai module new <name> "<description>"` scaffolds `module.md`, a
   hello-world `argc.sh` and `tests/<name>.bats` in `.skogai/modules/<name>/`
   (`--to global` for `~/.config/skogai/modules/`).
2. fill in `module.md`: `tools`, `files`, `config` defaults, and a body that
   explains every key.
3. write the recipes in `argc.sh` (argc spec: core's `docs/argc/specification.md`).
4. write its tests, then `skogai module test <name>`: the contracts and its
   own tests pass.
5. to ship it with a plugin, move the directory to the plugin's `modules/`.
   it is then a `source` everywhere the plugin is enabled.

## open

- modules shipped by plugins other than this one: how their `modules/` get
  onto `SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH`.
- `module update`: pulling source changes into an installed copy, file by
  file, `keep` respected.
- versions in `module.md`, and `requires` with versions.
- `command` as any executable, not only argc.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @describe skogai core: config across layers, and the modules skogai is made of
#
# a module is a directory with a module.md: frontmatter says what it is, which
# argc script is its command, which files it offers and its config defaults.
# modules are found installed (local .skogai/modules, then global), then in
# the sources on $SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH. the first one by a name wins.
# @meta require-tools git,yq
# @meta binname skogai
# @env SKOGAI_SYSTEM_DIR=/etc/skogai  dir of the system layer config
# @env SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR  dir of the global layer, default ~/.config/skogai
# @env SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR=.skogai  dir of the local layer; relative is from the git root, or pwd
# @env SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH  colon-separated dirs of module sources, default the one this module sits in

# shellcheck disable=SC2154 # argc_* are assigned by --argc-eval
set -euo pipefail

SELF="$(realpath "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
GLOBAL_DIR="${SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/skogai}"
MODULE_PATH="${SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH:-$(dirname "$(dirname "$SELF")")}"

# joins the items of a list value; `get` prints one item per line
SEP=$'\x1f'

# @cmd read and write key/value config across system, global, local and module layers
#
# fold order, later wins: module.md `config:` defaults, system, global, local,
# module.local.md overrides, --file layers, then SKOGAI_* env.
# a module's keys are mounted under its name: runner's `model` is `runner.model`.
config() { :; }

# @cmd print the resolved value of a key; a list prints one item per line
# @flag --show-origin  also print which layer the value came from
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
# @arg key![`_choice_key`]
config::get() {
    local line
    line="$(_line "$argc_key")" || exit $?
    if [[ ${argc_show_origin:-} == 1 ]]; then
        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(cut -f3 <<<"$line")" "$(cut -f2 <<<"$line" | tr "$SEP" ' ')"
    else
        cut -f2 <<<"$line" | tr "$SEP" '\n'
    fi
}

# @cmd set a key in the local layer, the global one, a module's module.local.md or a --file's .local.md
# @flag --global  write to the global layer instead of local
# @option --module[`_choice_module`]  write this module's module.local.md
# @option --file  write this file's .local.md frontmatter instead
# @option --scope  the section --file keys are mounted under
# @arg key![?`_choice_key`]
# @arg value!
config::set() {
    local file key
    if _md_target; then
        key="$(_file_key "$argc_key")" || exit 2
        [[ -f $file ]] || { mkdir -p "$(dirname "$file")" && printf -- '---\n{}\n---\n' >"$file"; }
        K="$key" V="$argc_value" \
            yq -i --front-matter=process 'setpath(strenv(K) | split("."); strenv(V) | from_yaml)' "$file"
        return
    fi
    file="$(_target_file)"
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$file")"
    git config -f "$file" "$argc_key" "$argc_value"
}

# @cmd remove a key from the local layer, the global one, a module's module.local.md or a --file's .local.md
# @flag --global  remove from the global layer instead of local
# @option --module[`_choice_module`]  remove from this module's module.local.md
# @option --file  remove from this file's .local.md frontmatter instead
# @option --scope  the section --file keys are mounted under
# @arg key![`_choice_target_key`]
config::unset() {
    local file key
    if _md_target; then
        key="$(_file_key "$argc_key")" || exit 2
        [[ -f $file ]] || exit 1
        K="$key" \
            yq -i --front-matter=process 'delpaths([strenv(K) | split(".")])' "$file"
        return
    fi
    file="$(_target_file)"
    [[ -f $file ]] || exit 1
    git config -f "$file" --unset-all "$argc_key" || exit 1
}

# @cmd print every resolved key as key=value; a list prints one line per item
# @flag --show-origin  prefix each line with the layer it came from
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
config::list() {
    local key value origin item resolved
    resolved="$(_resolve)" || exit 2
    [[ -n $resolved ]] || return 0
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value origin; do
        while IFS= read -r -d "$SEP" item; do
            if [[ ${argc_show_origin:-} == 1 ]]; then
                printf '%s\t%s=%s\n' "$origin" "$key" "$item"
            else
                printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$item"
            fi
        done <<<"$value$SEP"
    done <<<"$resolved"
}

# @cmd print the resolved config as export lines; a list's items are newline-separated
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
config::env() {
    local key value origin resolved
    resolved="$(_resolve)" || exit 2
    [[ -n $resolved ]] || return 0
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value origin; do
        printf 'export %s=%q\n' "$(_env_name "$key")" "${value//$SEP/$'\n'}"
    done <<<"$resolved"
}

# @cmd print the path of each layer file, and whether it exists
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  accepted for symmetry with get and list; unused
config::files() {
    local layer file name dir
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        _present "module:$name" "$dir/module.md"
    done < <(_modules)
    for layer in system global local; do
        _present "$layer" "$(_layer_file "$layer")"
    done
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        _present "module:$name" "$(_module_local_md "$name" "$layer" "$dir")"
    done < <(_modules)
    while IFS= read -r file; do
        _present file "$file"
    done < <(_file_layers)
}

# @cmd find, show, install and scaffold modules
module() { :; }

# @cmd every module by name: where it was found and what it is
module::ls() {
    local name layer dir
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        printf '%-12s %-7s %s\n' "$name" "$layer" "$(_field "$dir/module.md" .description)"
    done < <(_modules)
}

# @cmd a module's manifest, where it lives, and what it is missing
# @arg name![`_choice_module`]
module::show() {
    local dir layer
    IFS=$'\t' read -r _ layer dir < <(_module "$argc_name") || { echo "no module: $argc_name" >&2; exit 1; }
    printf '%s\t%s\n' "$layer" "$dir"
    yq --front-matter=extract . "$dir/module.md"
    _missing "$dir"
}

# @cmd path of a module's argc script; exits 1 if it has none
# @arg name![`_choice_module`]
module::command() {
    local dir
    IFS=$'\t' read -r _ _ dir < <(_module "$argc_name") || exit 1
    module::command_of "$dir"
}

# a module dir's argc script, or 1 if it has none
module::command_of() {
    local cmd
    cmd="$(_field "$1/module.md" .command)"
    [[ -n $cmd && -f $1/$cmd ]] || return 1
    echo "$1/$cmd"
}

# @cmd run modules' tests with bats: the contracts of what it requires, then the module's own tests/
#
# every module you require runs its contract against you: core's
# tests/contract.bats, and tests/contract.bats of each module in `requires`
# that has one. its own tests/*.bats, but its contract.bats, run after; they
# load core's tests/helper.bash for an isolated repo and layers.
# tests, contracts and the helper come from the source when there is one, else where it is found.
# @arg module*[`_choice_module`]  default every module found
# @option --filter  only tests whose name matches this regex
module::test() {
    : "${SKOGAI_BIN:?run me as skogai module test}"
    command -v bats >/dev/null || { echo "bats is not on PATH" >&2; exit 2; }
    local core name dir r rdir rc=0 files names=("${argc_module[@]}")
    core="$(_source core)" || IFS=$'\t' read -r _ _ core < <(_module core)
    [[ ${#names[@]} -gt 0 ]] || mapfile -t names < <(_modules | cut -f1)
    for name in "${names[@]}"; do
        dir="$(_source "$name")" || IFS=$'\t' read -r _ _ dir < <(_module "$name") ||
            { echo "no module: $name" >&2; rc=1; continue; }
        files=("$core/tests/contract.bats")
        while IFS= read -r r; do
            [[ -n $r && $r != core ]] || continue
            rdir="$(_source "$r")" || IFS=$'\t' read -r _ _ rdir < <(_module "$r") || continue
            [[ ! -f $rdir/tests/contract.bats ]] || files+=("$rdir/tests/contract.bats")
        done < <(_field "$dir/module.md" '.requires[]')
        [[ ! -d $dir/tests ]] || mapfile -t -O "${#files[@]}" files < <(find "$dir/tests" -name '*.bats' ! -path "$dir/tests/contract.bats" | sort)
        echo "# $name" >&2
        # the module under test is a source in its isolated repo, wherever it was found
        SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH="$(dirname "$dir"):$MODULE_PATH" \
            SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE="$name" SKOGAI_TEST_HELPER="$core/tests/helper.bash" \
            bats ${argc_filter:+--filter "$argc_filter"} "${files[@]}" || rc=1
    done
    return "$rc"
}

# @cmd build `skogai` for a shell: one argc file with every module, man pages, completions
#
# writes into <local|global dir>/tmp/skogai/, throwaway and rebuilt at will:
# bin/skogai (help and completion for core and every module found from here;
# everything runs through the bin/skogai that built it), completions/skogai.sh
# for ARGC_COMPLETIONS_PATH, completions/skogai.{bash,zsh,fish}, man/man1.
# prints the env lines that put it on PATH, MANPATH and ARGC_COMPLETIONS_PATH.
# @option --to[local|global]  where to build, default core.module.install
# @option --shell[bash|zsh|fish]  env lines for this shell, default from $SHELL
module::build() {
    : "${SKOGAI_BIN:?run me as skogai module build}"
    local to out tmp name layer dir cmd shell
    to="${argc_to:-$(_get core.module.install local)}"
    out="$(dirname "$(_install_dir "$to")")/tmp/skogai"
    tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' RETURN
    mkdir -p "$tmp/bin" "$tmp/completions" "$tmp/man/man1"
    _main >"$tmp/bin/skogai"
    chmod +x "$tmp/bin/skogai"
    argc --argc-export "$tmp/bin/skogai" >/dev/null
    cp "$tmp/bin/skogai" "$tmp/completions/skogai.sh"
    for shell in bash zsh fish; do argc --argc-completions "$shell" skogai >"$tmp/completions/skogai.$shell"; done
    # core and every module give their own pages; the main file only skogai.1, the list
    argc --argc-mangen "$SELF" "$tmp/man/man1" >/dev/null
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        [[ $name != core ]] || continue
        cmd="$(module::command_of "$dir")" || continue
        argc --argc-mangen "$cmd" "$tmp/man/man1" >/dev/null
    done < <(_modules)
    mkdir "$tmp/main" && argc --argc-mangen "$tmp/bin/skogai" "$tmp/main" >/dev/null && cp "$tmp/main/skogai.1" "$tmp/man/man1/"
    rm -rf "$tmp/main"
    for f in "$tmp/man/man1"/*' '*; do [[ -e $f ]] && mv "$f" "${f// /-}"; done
    rm -rf "$out"
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$out")"
    cp -r "$tmp" "$out"
    echo "built $out" >&2
    shell="${argc_shell:-$(basename "${SHELL:-bash}")}"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # lines for the user's shell, expanded there
    case "$shell" in
    fish)
        printf 'fish_add_path --prepend %q\n' "$out/bin"
        printf 'set -gx MANPATH %q $MANPATH\n' "$out/man"
        printf 'set -gx ARGC_COMPLETIONS_PATH %q $ARGC_COMPLETIONS_PATH\n' "$out/completions"
        printf 'source %q\n' "$out/completions/skogai.fish"
        ;;
    *)
        printf 'export PATH=%q:"$PATH"\n' "$out/bin"
        printf 'export MANPATH=%q:"$MANPATH"\n' "$out/man"
        printf 'export ARGC_COMPLETIONS_PATH=%q:"$ARGC_COMPLETIONS_PATH"\n' "$out/completions"
        printf 'source %q\n' "$out/completions/skogai.$shell"
        ;;
    esac
}

# @cmd an empty skogai to try things in: own layers, every module installed, skogai built
#
# makes <dir>/system and <dir>/global (the system and global layers) and a
# git repo <dir>/repo, installs every module found from here into its
# .skogai/modules (as `module add --apply` would, from its source when it has
# one, else from where it was found) and builds skogai there.
# prints the env lines that switch a shell into it: no SKOGAI_* config from
# outside, the three layer dirs, the built skogai first on PATH, cd to repo.
# a dir made by an earlier sandbox is replaced; any other existing one is refused.
# @arg dir  default $TMPDIR/skogai
# @option --shell[bash|zsh|fish]  env lines for this shell, default from $SHELL
module::sandbox() {
    : "${SKOGAI_BIN:?run me as skogai module sandbox}"
    local dir shell name src v lines
    dir="${argc_dir:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/skogai}"
    [[ $dir == /* ]] || dir="${ARGC_PWD:-$PWD}/$dir"
    if [[ -f $dir/.sandbox ]]; then
        rm -rf "$dir"
    elif [[ -e $dir ]]; then
        echo "exists and is not a sandbox: $dir" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    mkdir -p "$dir/system" "$dir/global" "$dir/repo"
    touch "$dir/.sandbox"
    git -C "$dir/repo" init -q
    shell="${argc_shell:-$(basename "${SHELL:-bash}")}"
    # every run below sees only the sandbox's layers
    sandboxed() {
        (cd "$dir/repo" && SKOGAI_SYSTEM_DIR="$dir/system" SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR="$dir/global" \
            SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR="$dir/repo/.skogai" "$SKOGAI_BIN" "$@")
    }
    local found
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name _ found; do
        src="$(_source "$name")" || src="$found"
        sandboxed module add "$src" --to local --apply >/dev/null
    done < <(_modules)
    lines="$(sandboxed module build --to local --shell "$shell")"
    _sandbox_run "$dir" >"$dir/run"

# @cmd check modules against the spec (docs/module.md), all found ones if none given
#
# one line per problem: name, error or warn, message. exit 1 on any error;
# a missing tool is a warn, it is about this machine, not the module.
# @arg module*[?`_choice_module`]  names, or paths to module dirs
module::check() {
    local m dir rc=0 targets=("${argc_module[@]}")
    [[ ${#targets[@]} -gt 0 ]] || mapfile -t targets < <(_modules | cut -f3)
    for m in "${targets[@]}"; do
        if [[ $m == */* || $m == . ]]; then
            dir="$(cd "${ARGC_PWD:-$PWD}" && realpath "$m")"
        else
            IFS=$'\t' read -r _ _ dir < <(_module "$m") || { printf '%s\terror\tnot found\n' "$m"; rc=1; continue; }
        fi
        _check "$dir" || rc=1
    done
    return "$rc"
}

# @cmd the env a module's command runs with, as export lines
#
# SKOGAI_MODULE, SKOGAI_MODULE_DIR, SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR and SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR
# (both absolute), and the module's own resolved keys: runner.model is
# SKOGAI_RUNNER_MODEL.
# @arg name![`_choice_module`]
module::env() {
    local dir key value
    IFS=$'\t' read -r _ _ dir < <(_module "$argc_name") || exit 1
    printf 'export SKOGAI_MODULE=%q\n' "$argc_name"
    printf 'export SKOGAI_MODULE_DIR=%q\n' "$dir"
    printf 'export SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR=%q\n' "$(_local_dir)"
    printf 'export SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR=%q\n' "$GLOBAL_DIR"
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value _; do
        [[ $key == "$argc_name".* ]] || continue
        printf 'export %s=%q\n' "$(_env_name "$key")" "${value//$SEP/$'\n'}"
    done < <(_resolve)
}

# @cmd copy a module into .skogai/modules, or the global dir. prints the plan unless --apply
#
# copies module.md, its command and its `files:`. a file already there and
# different is kept and reported; `skogai module diff` shows how.
# exit 1 when there is something to copy and --apply was not given.
# @arg source![?`_choice_source`]  a module name from the sources, or a path to a module dir
# @option --to[local|global]  where to install, default core.module.install
# @flag --apply  copy the files
module::add() {
    local src name to dest rel status todo=0
    src="$(_source "$argc_source")" || { echo "no module source: $argc_source" >&2; exit 2; }
    name="$(basename "$src")"
    to="${argc_to:-$(_get core.module.install local)}"
    dest="$(_install_dir "$to")/$name"
    [[ $src != "$dest" ]] || { echo "already installed: $dest" >&2; exit 0; }
    echo "$name: $src -> $dest" >&2
    while IFS= read -r rel; do
        if [[ ! -e $dest/$rel ]]; then
            status=add todo=1
        elif cmp -s "$src/$rel" "$dest/$rel"; then
            status=same
        else
            status=keep
        fi
        printf '%-5s %s\n' "$status" "$rel"
        if [[ $status == add && ${argc_apply:-} == 1 ]]; then
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest/$rel")"
            cp -p "$src/$rel" "$dest/$rel"
        fi
    done < <(_module_files "$src")
    _missing "$src" >&2
    [[ $todo == 0 || ${argc_apply:-} == 1 ]] || exit 1
}

# @cmd diff an installed module against its source
# @arg name![`_choice_installed`]
module::diff() {
    local dir src rel rc=0
    IFS=$'\t' read -r _ _ dir < <(_module "$argc_name") || exit 1
    src="$(_source "$argc_name")" || { echo "no source for $argc_name" >&2; exit 2; }
    while IFS= read -r rel; do
        diff -u --label "source/$rel" --label "installed/$rel" "$src/$rel" "$dir/$rel" 2>/dev/null || rc=1
    done < <(_module_files "$src")
    return "$rc"
}

# @cmd scaffold a new module from core's templates/module
# @arg name!  lowercase, one segment
# @arg description  what it is, one line
# @option --to[local|global]  where to create it, default core.module.install
module::new() {
    [[ $argc_name =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$ ]] || { echo "bad name: $argc_name" >&2; exit 2; }
    ! _reserved "$argc_name" || { echo "reserved: $argc_name" >&2; exit 2; }
    local to dest core tpl f
    to="${argc_to:-$(_get core.module.install local)}"
    dest="$(_install_dir "$to")/$argc_name"
    [[ ! -e $dest ]] || { echo "exists: $dest" >&2; exit 2; }
    IFS=$'\t' read -r _ _ core < <(_module core)
    tpl="$core/templates/module"
    while IFS= read -r f; do
        mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest/$f")"
        NAME="$argc_name" DESC="${argc_description:-}" \
            awk '{ gsub(/\{\{name\}\}/, ENVIRON["NAME"]); gsub(/\{\{description\}\}/, ENVIRON["DESC"]); gsub(/\{\{NAME\}\}/, toupper(ENVIRON["NAME"])); print }' \
            "$tpl/$f" >"$dest/${f//_name_/$argc_name}"
        [[ ! -x $tpl/$f ]] || chmod +x "$dest/${f//_name_/$argc_name}"
        echo "wrote $dest/${f//_name_/$argc_name}" >&2
    done < <(cd "$tpl" && find . -type f -printf '%P\n' | sort)
}

# the resolved "key<TAB>value<TAB>origin" line of a key; exit 1 if unset
_line() {
    local resolved
    resolved="$(_resolve)" || return 2
    awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" '$1 == k { print; f = 1 } END { exit !f }' <<<"$resolved"
}

# a resolved value, or $2 if unset
_get() { _line "$1" | cut -f2 | grep . || echo "${2:-}"; }

_local_dir() {
    local dir="${SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR:-.skogai}"
    [[ $dir == /* ]] || dir="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)/$dir"
    echo "$dir"
}

_install_dir() {
    case "$1" in
    local) echo "$(_local_dir)/modules" ;;
    global) echo "$GLOBAL_DIR/modules" ;;
    *) echo "bad --to: $1" >&2; return 2 ;;
    esac
}

# "layer<TAB>dir" for every place modules are looked for, in order
_module_bases() {
    local p
    printf 'local\t%s\n' "$(_install_dir local)"
    printf 'global\t%s\n' "$(_install_dir global)"
    IFS=: read -ra p <<<"$MODULE_PATH"
    for p in "${p[@]}"; do [[ -z $p ]] || printf 'source\t%s\n' "$p"; done
}

# "name<TAB>layer<TAB>dir" for every module, the first by a name wins
_modules() {
    local -A seen
    local layer base d name
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r layer base; do
        for d in "$base"/*/; do
            [[ -f $d/module.md ]] || continue
            d="$(realpath "$d")"
            name="$(basename "$d")"
            [[ -z ${seen[$name]:-} ]] || continue
            seen[$name]=1
            printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$name" "$layer" "$d"
        done
    done < <(_module_bases)
}

_module() { _modules | awk -F'\t' -v n="$1" '$1 == n { print; f = 1 } END { exit !f }'; }

# a module dir to install from: a path, or a name looked up in the sources only
_source() {
    local p
    if [[ $1 == */* || $1 == . ]]; then
        p="$(cd "${ARGC_PWD:-$PWD}" && realpath -e "$1")" && [[ -f $p/module.md ]] && echo "$p"
        return
    fi
    _module_bases | while IFS=$'\t' read -r layer p; do
        [[ $layer == source && -f $p/$1/module.md ]] && { realpath "$p/$1"; break; }
    done | grep .
}

# files a module consists of, relative to its dir: module.md, its command, its `files:`
_module_files() {
    local dir="$1" f
    {
        echo module.md
        _field "$dir/module.md" .command
        while IFS= read -r f; do
            [[ -n $f ]] || continue
            if [[ -d $dir/$f ]]; then (cd "$dir" && find "${f%/}" -type f); else echo "$f"; fi
        done < <(_field "$dir/module.md" '.files[]')
    } | grep . | sort -u
}

# the main argc file for `module build`: templates/main.sh with one forwarding
# recipe per core group and per module with a command between its markers
_main() {
    local tpl name layer dir cmd desc known=config\|module\|help
    tpl="$(dirname "$SELF")/templates/main.sh"
    sed '/^# >>> generated$/q' "$tpl"
    printf 'BIN=%q\nCORE=%q\ndeclare -A CMDS=()\n' "$SKOGAI_BIN" "$SELF"
    for name in config module; do
        desc="$(argc --argc-export "$SELF" | N="$name" yq -p json '.subcommands[] | select(.name == strenv(N)) | .describe | split("\n") | .[0]')"
        _forward "$name" "$desc"
    done
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        [[ $name != core ]] || continue
        cmd="$(module::command_of "$dir")" || continue
        printf 'CMDS[%s]=%q\n' "$name" "$cmd"
        _forward "$name" "$(_field "$dir/module.md" .description)"
        known+="|$name"

if [[ ! -f $dir/$f ]]; then
            _bad "command $f is missing"
        else
            argc --argc-export "$dir/$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 || _bad "command $f does not parse with argc"
        fi
    fi
    for t in tools requires files; do
        [[ $(yq --front-matter=extract ".$t | tag" "$md") =~ ^\!\!(seq|null)$ ]] || _bad "$t is not a list"
    done
    [[ $(yq --front-matter=extract '.config | tag' "$md") =~ ^\!\!(map|null)$ ]] || _bad "config is not a map"
    while IFS= read -r f; do
        [[ -z $f || -e $dir/$f ]] || _bad "file $f is missing"
    done < <(_field "$md" '.files[]')
    [[ $name == core ]] || _field "$md" '.requires[]' | grep -qx core || _bad "does not require core"
    while IFS= read -r r; do
        [[ -z $r ]] || _module "$r" >/dev/null || _bad "requires $r, not found"
    done < <(_field "$md" '.requires[]')
    while IFS= read -r t; do
        [[ -z $t ]] || command -v "$t" >/dev/null || printf '%s\twarn\ttool %s not on PATH\n' "$name" "$t"
    done < <(_field "$md" '.tools[]')
    compgen -G "$dir/tests/*.bats" >/dev/null || printf '%s\twarn\tno tests/*.bats\n' "$name"
    while IFS= read -r f; do
        printf '%s\twarn\tunknown field %s\n' "$name" "$f"
    done < <(yq --front-matter=extract 'keys | .[] | select(test("^(type|name|description|command|tools|requires|files|config)$") | not)' "$md")
    return "$err"
}

# tools and modules a module dir needs and can't find, one line each
_missing() {
    local t r
    while IFS= read -r t; do
        [[ -z $t ]] || command -v "$t" >/dev/null || echo "missing tool: $t"
    done < <(_field "$1/module.md" '.tools[]')
    while IFS= read -r r; do
        [[ -z $r ]] || _module "$r" >/dev/null || echo "missing module: $r (skogai module add $r)"
    done < <(_field "$1/module.md" '.requires[]')
}

# a frontmatter field, empty if missing
_field() { yq --front-matter=extract "$2 // \"\"" "$1" 2>/dev/null || true; }

_present() { printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$2" "$([[ -f $2 ]] && echo present || echo missing)"; }

# layers in fold order, later wins: system, global, local
_layer_file() {
    case "$1" in
    system) echo "$SKOGAI_SYSTEM_DIR/config" ;;
    global) echo "$GLOBAL_DIR/config" ;;
    local) echo "$(_local_dir)/config" ;;
    esac
}

# x.md -> x.local.md
_local_md() { echo "${1%.md}.local.md"; }

# a module's overrides: beside its module.md when installed; a source one's
# go in the local install dir, never into the source
_module_local_md() {
    if [[ $2 == source ]]; then echo "$(_install_dir local)/$1/module.local.md"; else echo "$3/module.local.md"; fi
}

# --file layers in fold order: each x.md, then its x.local.md
_file_layers() {
    local f
    for f in "${argc_file[@]}"; do
        echo "$f"
        _local_md "$f"
    done
}

# set/unset into a markdown file: sets `file`, and `argc_scope` for --module
_md_target() {
    if [[ -n ${argc_module:-} ]]; then
        local layer dir
        IFS=$'\t' read -r _ layer dir < <(_module "$argc_module") || { echo "no module: $argc_module" >&2; exit 2; }
        file="$(_module_local_md "$argc_module" "$layer" "$dir")"
        argc_scope="$argc_module"
        MD_ROOT=config
        return 0
    fi
    [[ -n ${argc_file:-} ]] || return 1
    file="$(_local_md "$argc_file")"
}

# `.` is a relation, `-` is part of a name: stage.on-stop -> SKOGAI_STAGE_ONSTOP
_env_name() {
    local k="${1^^}"
    k="${k//-/}"
    echo "SKOGAI_${k//./_}"
}

# a frontmatter file as "key<TAB>tag<TAB>value" lines: nested maps flatten to
# dotted keys, under the scope ($2, or --scope) if given, with `_` read as `-`.
# $3 picks the map to read, default the whole frontmatter. a list is one value,
# its items joined by SEP.
_frontmatter() {
    yq --front-matter=extract "select(document_index == 0) | ${3:-.} // {}" "$1" |
        SEP="$SEP" SCOPE="${2-${argc_scope:-}}" yq '
        select(tag == "!!map") | .. |
        select(tag == "!!seq" or (tag != "!!map" and (parent | tag) != "!!seq")) |
        [ ((strenv(SCOPE) | select(. != "") | [.]) // []) + path | join(".") | downcase | sub("_"; "-"),
          tag,
          (select(tag == "!!seq") | map(tostring) | join(strenv(SEP))) // tostring
        ] | join("\t")'
}

# prints "key<TAB>value<TAB>origin" for every resolved key
_resolve() {
    local -A val origin
    local layer file key value env tag name dir fm entry
    _fold() { # file scope root origin
        [[ -f $1 ]] || return 0
        fm="$(_frontmatter "$1" "$2" "$3")" || exit 2
        while IFS=$'\t' read -r key tag value; do
            [[ -n $key ]] || continue
            if [[ $tag == '!!null' ]]; then
                builtin unset "val[$key]" "origin[$key]"
            else
                val[$key]="$value"
                origin[$key]="$4"
            fi
        done <<<"$fm"
    }
    local mods
    mods="$(_modules)"
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        [[ -z $name ]] || _fold "$dir/module.md" "$name" .config "module:$name"
    done <<<"$mods"
    for layer in system global local; do
        file="$(_layer_file "$layer")"
        [[ -f $file ]] || continue
        while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
            key="${entry%%$'\n'*}"
            value="${entry#*$'\n'}"
            [[ $entry == *$'\n'* ]] || value=""
            val[$key]="$value"
            origin[$key]="$layer"
        done < <(git config -f "$file" --list -z)
    done
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        [[ -z $name ]] || _fold "$(_module_local_md "$name" "$layer" "$dir")" "$name" .config "module:$name.local"
    done <<<"$mods"
    while IFS= read -r file; do
        _fold "$file" "${argc_scope:-}" . "file:$file"
    done < <(_file_layers)
    for key in "${!val[@]}"; do
        env="$(_env_name "$key")"
        if [[ -n ${!env+x} ]]; then
            val[$key]="${!env}"
            origin[$key]="env:$env"
        fi
    done
    for key in "${!val[@]}"; do
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$key" "${val[$key]}" "${origin[$key]}"
    done | sort
}

_target_file() {
    if [[ ${argc_global:-} == 1 ]]; then _layer_file global; else _layer_file local; fi
}

# every resolved key, only --module's own if given; choices for get and set,
# described by value when completing
_choice_key() {
    local keys
    keys="$(_resolve | awk -F'\t' -v m="${argc_module:-}" 'm == "" || index($1, m ".") == 1')"
    if [[ ${ARGC_COMPGEN:-0} == 1 ]]; then cut -f1,2 <<<"$keys" | tr "$SEP" ' '; else cut -f1 <<<"$keys"; fi
}

# keys present in the layer set/unset write to; choices for unset
_choice_target_key() {
    local file
    if _md_target 2>/dev/null; then
        if [[ -f $file ]]; then _frontmatter "$file" "${argc_scope:-}" "${MD_ROOT:+.$MD_ROOT}" | cut -f1; fi
    else
        file="$(_target_file)"
        if [[ -f $file ]]; then git config -f "$file" --name-only --list; fi
    fi
}

_choice_module() { _modules | cut -f1; }
_choice_installed() { _modules | awk -F'\t' '$2 != "source" { print $1 }'; }
_choice_source() { _module_bases | awk -F'\t' '$1 == "source" { print $2 }' | while read -r p; do ls "$p"; done | sort -u; }

# the frontmatter path of a key in a markdown layer: the key minus its scope,
# under `config.` for a module's module.local.md
_file_key() {
    local key="$1" scope="${argc_scope:-}"
    if [[ -n $scope ]]; then
        [[ $key == "$scope".* ]] || { echo "key $key is outside $scope" >&2; return 2; }
        key="${key#"$scope".}"
    fi
    [[ $key =~ ^[^.]+(\.[^.]+)*$ ]] || { echo "bad key: $1" >&2; return 2; }
    echo "${MD_ROOT:+$MD_ROOT.}$key"
}

# Context Summary

Persistent record of architectural decisions, discovered patterns, gotchas, and active context.
This file is referenced in CLAUDE.md and loaded every session.

## Active Context
- Steps 1-2 done (F001 checker, F002 staged Podman run). usage + mise is the interface; argc twins frozen (2026-11-06).
- Landed 2026-11-06: run events (`docs/evidence.md`), live-test examples (`tests/examples.bats`), `mise run test` on usage. Next: a second module that `depends_on` hello; step 3 leftovers (recovery, reader, workorder link).
- Not implemented: the workorder lifecycle through the runner (agents still edit the repo directly), `depends_on` at run time, config precedence.

## Cross-Cutting Concerns
- Stack: bash + argc, tests in bats, tools managed via mise (`latest`, not pinned) (argc, jq, yq, bats); Arch container (`mise run test:container`) and PKGBUILD in `packaging/arch/`
- Intended architecture: skogai-runner will provide the single entrypoint for skogai 3.0 init/setup/bootstrap/install. `src/core/` holds system-level modules (think /etc/skogai, /usr/share/skogai); `.skogai/` is userspace / local override. argc is the interface for both user and agents.
- Key constraints: lowercase single-segment names; no sed/awk in the core template; trust existing tools (pacman, git, mise) instead of reinventing.

## Domain: core runner

### Decisions
- bash + argc chosen: argc gives one declarative CLI surface (help, completion, parsing) usable by humans and agents alike (2026-10-29)
- `best-version-so-far/` contains active module plans and reusable implementation. Foundation work comes first; tasks may reuse it deliberately. `agents/` and `docs/argc*` also contain reference material. Earlier validation claims need rechecking (clarified 2026-10-29)

- F001 is the relationship contract checker only (spec-gated 2026-10-30). Invalid input is a verdict (JSONL on stdout, exit 0); exit 2 bad args, exit 1 missing yq/jq. Old proposals (split main.sh, .skogai override, single binary) deferred per docs/plan.md (2026-10-30)
- Open plan-step-1 items, not yet features: operation identity / retry / linked intent revisions; configuration ownership and precedence (mise vs git config vs env vs module defaults). Step 2 writable-scope enforcement decided by skogix (2026-11-06): Podman, staged output. The command runs in Podman with the repo mounted read-only (as `mise run test:container` does) plus one empty writable output dir; the runner then verifies the output dir holds only paths in `owns` and only then moves them into place atomically. Out-of-scope writes are impossible inside the container (ro mount) and out-of-scope outputs are rejected before any effect. Implemented as F002 (2026-11-06): src/core/run/argc.sh check|run, example examples/hello.
- usage twins (2026-11-06): to compare argc with usage + mise, every argc piece has a usage twin with the same behavior and tests: `contract/usage.sh`, `run/usage.sh` (+ `examples/usage/hello`, `tests/fixtures/run-usage`), and `main-usage.sh` (`skogai`: no template/sync, usage `mount` reads the registry live; `SKOGAI_COMMANDS` is a `:`-list of registry layers, nearest first). Not spec-gated features; no entry in features.json. Until the comparison is decided, a change to a rule, runner, example or fixture goes into both twins. Open for skogix: criteria and decision for argc vs usage, and whether packaging (PKGBUILD) ships `skogai`.

- usage + mise chosen over argc as the interface for user, agents and modules (skogix, 2026-11-06). New work goes into the usage files only; the argc files are frozen, not removed. Why: one interface instead of twinning every change; usage gives layered registries (`SKOGAI_COMMANDS`), `effect=` for agents via `usage mcp`, and mise integration.
- Evidence starts from the skogai-core hook log shape (`/home/skogix/skogai/.skogai/logs/skogai-core/log.jsonl`: `{ts, event, action?, input}`), extended with run identity and outcome, not a new format (2026-11-06).

### Patterns
- Tests isolate HOME under `$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR` and drive the template via `argc --argc-run`.

### Gotchas
- Rootless podman finds its images through XDG_DATA_HOME (default $HOME/.local/share). Tests that isolate HOME must capture and export XDG_DATA_HOME first, or `podman image exists` fails. This host exports XDG_DATA_HOME already, which hides the problem.
- Do not add `:Z` to podman mounts of module dirs: SELinux relabelling changes the host directory, which is an effect outside `owns`.
- The runner logs to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/skogai/run.jsonl`. This host exports XDG_STATE_HOME, so isolating HOME alone leaks test runs into the real log: tests must set XDG_STATE_HOME and unset SKOGAI_LOG.
- Workorder agents in worktrees under ~/skogai-runner/.claude/worktrees: a hook refuses plain `git` (rtk wrapper); they used `/usr/bin/git`. `mise tasks` there also picks up the parent checkout's mise.toml.
- `mise run test` stays on argc for the twinned files; `mise run test:usage` runs contract.bats and run.bats with `CONTRACT_IMPL=usage RUN_IMPL=usage` plus main-usage.bats. Both suites must pass after a twinned change.
- `contract/usage.sh` receives the variadic `file` as one shell-quoted string (`eval "files=(...)"`); under a usage mount, `usage_cmd` is the mounted script's `bin`, so main-usage.sh dispatches on argv.
- `mise run test` now depends on `mise run image` (cached `podman build`, a no-op without podman).
- No coverage tooling for bash/bats yet: the 95% coverage gate cannot be measured. `full_test` runs `bats tests` only. Enabling coverage (e.g. bashcov/kcov) needs its own feature if wanted.
- `ssh -T git@github.com` fails (no key loaded); remote is HTTPS under `skogai2`. The identity hook checks name/email only.

## Meta-Patterns
<!-- Coordination insights that apply across features — NOT domain-specific.
     Populated by the retrospective step at session end. -->

tool_input.new_string:
- Module model and config answers (skogix, 2026-11-07). `best-version-so-far/` is the reference target (config fold, module env, install by copy); it is deleted once everything is converted.
  - A module is three things: key/value config defaults, a usage declaration (strictly typed input -> output), and relationships. Candidate shape: one mise file, e.g. `mise.<name>.toml` (format not settled).
  - Relationships: `owns` = creates and is responsible for; `writes` = edits, i.e. gives input to the owning module to react to or use; `watches` = on an event at x, hand the event to executable y.
  - The entrypoint runs a module from anywhere (e.g. local). Once its tests and rules pass, it is copied to global (`~/.config/skogai`) or system (`/etc/skogai`).
  - Precedence, later wins: module defaults, system, global, local, override, command parameters, env. Plain Unix CLI practice.
  - Types are deferred; later modules validate paths, ints and so on.
  - Key/env names: kebab-case. `-` is part of a word and dropped in env; `.` maps to `_`, so `a.b-c.d` = `SKOGAI_A_BC_D` and `SKOGAI_FOO_BAR` = `skogai.foo.bar`.
  - Each module defines its own env, injected when it runs (mise does this for tasks).
  - `depends_on` at run time = the called command is available, i.e. that module is installed.
  - Workorder paths are relative to the git root.
- Verified in mise 2026.10.17 (scratch, 2026-11-07): a task's `usage` field validates args (a missing `<who>` is refused); `MISE_ENV=<name>` loads `mise.<name>.toml`; `[_.skogai]` free-form keys are readable with `mise config get`; `mise.local.toml` overrides it. A plain `[env]` value beats the caller's env. `"{{ get_env(name='X', default='d') }}"` lets the caller's env win, which the precedence above needs.
- Evidence starts from the skogai-core hook log shape

## Your module idea, tried in mise

I built a small module as `mise.hello.toml` in the scratchpad, with mise 2026.10.17:

```toml
[env]                                   # config defaults
SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING = "{{ get_env(name='SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING', default='hi') }}"

[_.skogai]                              # relationships (mise's free-form namespace)
owns = ["greeting.txt"]

[tasks.hello]                           # the usage declaration
usage = 'arg "<who>"'
run = 'echo "${SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING} ${usage_who}" > greeting.txt'
```

- **The env-var catch:** a plain `[env]` value beats the caller's environment variable, which is the reverse of your order. Writing each default as `get_env(..., default=...)` fixes it. All three parts of your module definition fit in one mise file, and mise already does the parsing, the layering and the env injection.

# Context Summary

Persistent record of architectural decisions, discovered patterns, gotchas, and active context.
This file is referenced in CLAUDE.md and loaded every session.

## Active Context
- Steps 1-2 done (F001 checker, F002 staged Podman run). usage + mise is the interface; argc twins frozen (2026-11-06).
- Landed 2026-11-06: run events (`docs/evidence.md`), live-test examples (`tests/examples.bats`), `mise run test` on usage. Next: a second module that `depends_on` hello; step 3 leftovers (recovery, reader, workorder link).
- Not implemented: the workorder lifecycle through the runner (agents still edit the repo directly), `depends_on` at run time, config precedence.

## Cross-Cutting Concerns
- Stack: bash + argc, tests in bats, tools managed via mise (`latest`, not pinned) (argc, jq, yq, bats); Arch container (`mise run test:container`) and PKGBUILD in `packaging/arch/`
- Intended architecture: skogai-runner will provide the single entrypoint for skogai 3.0 init/setup/bootstrap/install. `src/core/` holds system-level modules (think /etc/skogai, /usr/share/skogai); `.skogai/` is userspace / local override. argc is the interface for both user and agents.
- Key constraints: lowercase single-segment names; no sed/awk in the core template; trust existing tools (pacman, git, mise) instead of reinventing.

## Domain: core runner

## A proposal for the module format (A)

**A module in source** is a directory:

```
hello/
  hello.toml     # mise config: [env] defaults, [tasks.hello] with its usage spec, [_.skogai.hello] relationships
  README.md      # what the module is, every key it has, what it owns (for people)
  SKOGAI.md      # optional: instructions for agents working on or with it
  tests/
```

**Installing a module copies `hello.toml` into the `conf.d/` of the chosen level.** That is `.mise/conf.d/` for local, `~/.config/mise/conf.d/` for global, and `/etc/mise/conf.d/` for system. This matches your decision 4, run from anywhere and copy up once tests pass, without new machinery. mise already folds system, global, local in your order, and `mise config ls` shows which file each setting came from. Uninstalling deletes the file.

On your item 2: I'd use **README.md** for the module's own description, because every tool and forge already shows it. **SKOGAI.md** would be the agent-facing file, so skogai never depends on AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and the rest. MODULE.md would be a third name that adds nothing. I'm treating `watches` as deferred.

## Two risks this shape brings

1. **Every installed module is always active.** All `conf.d` files load in every shell under that level, so every module's `[env]` and tasks are visible everywhere. Prefixing every key `SKOGAI_<MODULE>_` and every relationship `_.skogai.<module>` keeps them from colliding. It doesn't give "each module gets only its own env", though. `run` would have to pass only that module's keys into the container, which is the plan for D anyway.
2. **Overriding one key.** A later layer can override an env key: a local `hello.toml` beats the global one. For a task, the later definition replaces the whole task. I haven't checked how mise merges two files that define the same task, so A's spec has to pin it down.

Next step is to write A's spec on this shape and run it through the spec gate. It covers: the module directory, `hello` converted into it, the contract checker reading `[_.skogai.<name>]` from the toml, and the naming rules. The spec gate is a separate review agent that checks the spec is complete and testable before any code. Should I go ahead on this shape, or do you want to change the layout first?

#!/usr/bin/env -S usage bash
#USAGE bin "contract"
#USAGE about "check the relationships Markdown+ files declare in their frontmatter"
#USAGE long_about """
#USAGE one compact JSON verdict per file on stdout, in argument order. an invalid file is an answer, not a failure: exit 0 whenever every file got a verdict.
#USAGE
#USAGE exit 1: yq or jq missing, or yq is not mikefarah's yq v4 or newer (another program named yq would turn every file into invalid-yaml).
#USAGE
#USAGE exit 2: no files, or one is missing, a directory, or unreadable. stdout stays empty on both. reads only, writes nothing.
#USAGE """
#USAGE cmd "check" help="check each file, and the relationships between all of them" {
#USAGE   arg "[file]..." help="Markdown files with frontmatter" var=#true
#USAGE }
#
# the usage twin of argc.sh: same rules, same output, same exit codes. usage
# parses the comments above and exports usage_cmd and usage_file; argc.sh gets
# argc_* from --argc-eval instead. usage itself exits 1 when the command line
# does not fit the spec, and 181 when the spec is broken.

# shellcheck shell=bash disable=SC2154 # usage_* are exported by usage
set -euo pipefail

check() {
    local tool file version files=()
    # a variadic arg arrives as one shell-quoted string, not an array
    eval "files=(${usage_file:-})"
    for tool in yq jq; do
        command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || { printf 'missing tool: %s\n' "$tool" >&2; return 1; }
    done
    # mikefarah's yq v4+ prints "yq (https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/) version v4.x.y";
    # the python wrapper prints "yq 3.x" and mikefarah's v3 "yq version 3.x"
    version="$(command yq --version 2>&1)" || true
    version="${version%%$'\n'*}"
    [[ "$version" =~ ^yq\ \(https://github\.com/mikefarah/yq/?\)\ version\ v?([0-9]+)\. ]] &&
        ((BASH_REMATCH[1] >= 4)) ||
        { printf 'wrong yq: need mikefarah/yq v4 or newer, found: %s\n' "$version" >&2; return 1; }
    # usage runs the script where it was called, so no cd back to the caller
    ((${#files[@]})) || { printf 'usage: check <file>...\n' >&2; return 2; }
    for file in "${files[@]}"; do
        [[ -e "$file" ]] || { printf 'no such file: %s\n' "$file" >&2; return 2; }
        [[ ! -d "$file" ]] || { printf 'is a directory: %s\n' "$file" >&2; return 2; }
        [[ -r "$file" ]] || { printf 'unreadable: %s\n' "$file" >&2; return 2; }
    done
    for file in "${files[@]}"; do _frontmatter "$file"; done |
        command jq -cs --arg pwd "$PWD" "$VERDICTS"
}

# one record per file: {file, parse: <reason>|null, data: <frontmatter>|null}
_frontmatter() {
    local file="$1" lines i data
    mapfile -t lines <"$file"
    [[ ${#lines[@]} -gt 0 && "${lines[0]}" == --- ]] || { _record "$file" no-frontmatter; return; }
    for ((i = 1; i < ${#lines[@]}; i++)); do [[ "${lines[i]}" != --- ]] || break; done
    ((i < ${#lines[@]})) || { _record "$file" unterminated-frontmatter; return; }
    data="$(printf '%s\n' "${lines[@]:1:i-1}" | command yq -p yaml -o json -I0 '.' 2>/dev/null)" ||
        { _record "$file" invalid-yaml; return; }
    [[ "$(command jq -r type <<<"$data" 2>/dev/null)" == object ]] || { _record "$file" not-a-mapping; return; }
    _record "$file" "" "$data"
}

- `[_.skogai.<name>]` (mise's free-form `_` namespace): the relationship table. Allowed keys: description (string), depends_on (array of names), reads, writes, owns, watches (arrays of paths). - `[env]`: the module's config defaults. Every key must start with `SKOGAI_<NAME>_`, where <NAME> is the name uppercased with `-` removed (hello-world -> SKOGAI_HELLOWORLD_). Values are not checked (types are deferred).
- `[tasks.<name>]`: the module's command, with a `usage` string (its usage spec). Any other task must be named `<name>:<something>`.

- invalid-toml: yq cannot parse the file.
- no-declaration: no `_.skogai` table, or it is empty.
- multiple-declarations: `_.skogai` has more than one key.
- name-mismatch: the single key under `_.skogai` differs from the file name without `.toml`.
- env-outside-prefix: an `[env]` key without the module's prefix.
- missing-task: no `[tasks.<name>]`, or it has no string `usage`.
- task-outside-prefix: a task other than `<name>` that is not named `<name>:...`.

Paths in reads/writes/owns/watches are resolved as the checker resolves them today (relative to the declaring file's directory) for ownership-conflict; run-time path base is out of scope.

Out of scope: install/uninstall (C), config get/set (B), run executing the mise task (D), depends_on at run time (E), watches behaviour, value types.
EOF

+      "description": "Relationship contract checker, by example (plan step 1, relationships only). An argc script src/core/contract/argc.sh with command `check <file>...` reads each Markdown file's frontmatter: YAML between a first line exactly `---` and the next line exactly `---`, parsed with yq v4. Keys (names provisional): name (required string matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$), description (optional string), depends_on (list of module names, each matching the same pattern), reads, writes, owns, watches (lists of non-empty paths relative to the file's directory), defaults (optional mapping; contents unchecked, deferred).
Output: stdout is JSONL, one compact JSON object per argument in argument order: {"file": <path as given>, "verdict": "valid"|"invalid", "reasons": [...]}; reasons are unique, sorted, empty when valid. Invalid input is a verdict: exit 0 whenever every argument got a verdict. Exit 2, stderr diagnostic, empty stdout: no arguments, or any argument that does not exist, is a directory, or is unreadable. Exit 1, stderr diagnostic, empty stdout: yq or jq not on PATH; this is checked first, before arguments, so exit 1 wins over exit 2. Pure read: writes no files; repeated runs give byte-identical output.
Per-file reasons. Parse stage, which stops further checks so the parse reason is the only one: no-frontmatter (first line not `---`, including an empty file), unterminated-frontmatter (no closing `---`), invalid-yaml (yq rejects the block), not-a-mapping (block parses but is empty, a scalar, or a list). Field stage, all collected: unknown-key (top-level key not listed above); missing-name (name absent or null); wrong-type (name, description, a depends_on entry, or a path in reads/writes/owns/watches that is not a string, an empty-string path, a relationship key that is not a list, defaults not a mapping); invalid-name (the file's own name or any depends_on entry not matching the pattern); path-outside-scope (absolute path, or a path whose lexical normalisation leaves the file's directory; `.` itself is inside). Lexical normalisation, used everywhere paths are compared: collapse repeated slashes, drop trailing slashes, resolve `.` and `..` textually, never resolve symlinks; so "out/", "out//" and "./out" all equal "out"; write-not-owned (a writes entry whose normalised form does not exactly equal a normalised owns entry; owning a directory does not cover paths under it).
A value that gets wrong-type is excluded from every other check (invalid-name, path-outside-scope, write-not-owned, and all cross-file checks); a file whose name is wrong-type provides no name.
Cross-file reasons, over every file in the call that reached the field stage with a string name, valid or not: missing-dependency (a depends_on name provided by no such file; self-dependency and cycles are valid); duplicate-name (two distinct files declare the same name; each gets it); ownership-conflict (two distinct files own paths that are equal after resolving each against its own file's directory and lexical normalisation; each gets it). Files are distinct by lexically normalised absolute path, so the same file given twice, under any spelling, yields two objects identical apart from "file" and never conflicts with itself.

+      "description": "Module format v1: a module's declaration is a mise config file, and the contract checker reads it (plan step 1, settled with skogix 2026-11-07, see context_summary "Module model and config answers" and "mise conf.d").
Layout: a module in source is a directory <name>/ holding <name>.toml (a mise config file that is installed later as a conf.d drop-in, so its file name is the module name), README.md (what the module is, every key it sets, what it owns), optionally SKOGAI.md (agent-facing) and tests/. Installing, running and `watches` behaviour are out of scope (features C, D and later).
Declaration inside <name>.toml:
- `[_.skogai.<name>]` (mise's free-form `_` namespace): the relationship table. Allowed keys: description (string), depends_on (array of names), reads, writes, owns, watches (arrays of paths). Same type, name and path rules as the Markdown frontmatter today; `name` and `defaults` are not allowed inside the table (reason `unknown-key`): the name is the table key, and defaults are `[env]`.
- `[env]`: the module's config defaults. Every key must start with `SKOGAI_<NAME>_`, where <NAME> is the name uppercased with `-` removed (hello-world -> SKOGAI_HELLOWORLD_). Values are not checked (types are deferred).
- `[tasks.<name>]`: the module's command, with a `usage` string (its usage spec). Any other task must be named `<name>:<something>`.
Contract checker change, in src/core/contract/usage.sh only (contract/argc.sh is frozen): `check` accepts files ending in `.toml` alongside Markdown files, in one call, so cross-file rules (missing-dependency, duplicate-name, ownership-conflict) apply across both kinds. Only the parse stage is new: a .toml file is parsed with `yq -p toml -o json`, then turned into the same {file, parse, data} record the Markdown parse produces, where data is the `_.skogai.<name>` table plus {name: <name>}; the VERDICTS jq program applies unchanged, plus the new module-only rules below. Output shape and exit codes are unchanged. Markdown handling (used by workorders) is unchanged.
New reasons, each with a fixture directory that produces exactly that reason:
- invalid-toml: yq cannot parse the file.
- no-declaration: no `_.skogai` table, or it is empty.
- multiple-declarations: `_.skogai` has more than one key.
- name-mismatch: the single key under `_.skogai` differs from the file name without `.toml`.
- env-outside-prefix: an `[env]` key without the module's prefix.
- missing-task: no `[tasks.<name>]`, or it has no string `usage`.
- task-outside-prefix: a task other than `<name>` that is not named `<name>:...`.
A non-table `_.skogai.<name>` is `not-a-mapping`; an invalid table key is `invalid-name`.
Paths in reads/writes/owns/watches are resolved as the checker resolves them today (relative to the declaring file's directory) for ownership-conflict; run-time path base is out of scope.
Example: examples/modules/hello/ with hello.toml (owns and writes greeting.txt, env SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING with a get_env default so the caller's env wins, task hello with usage `arg "<who>"`) and README.md. It must be valid, and `MISE_ENV`-free use works: with the file copied into a scratch project's .mise/conf.d/, `mise run hello world` exits 0 (skip when mise is unavailable).
Docs: docs/module.md describes the layout, the declaration, the naming rules and the reasons, marked implemented/verified, and records the mise facts it relies on (conf.d at system/global/project level; [env] merges per key across layers; a task is replaced whole by a later layer, so only the module's own file defines its tasks and relationships, and override files set [env] only; `mise config get _.x` reads one file, no merge).

# Context Summary

Persistent record of architectural decisions, discovered patterns, gotchas, and active context.
This file is referenced in CLAUDE.md and loaded every session.

## Active Context
- Steps 1-2 done (F001 checker, F002 staged Podman run). usage + mise is the interface; argc twins frozen (2026-11-06).
- Landed 2026-11-06: run events (`docs/evidence.md`), live-test examples (`tests/examples.bats`), `mise run test` on usage. Next: a second module that `depends_on` hello; step 3 leftovers (recovery, reader, workorder link).
- Not implemented: the workorder lifecycle through the runner (agents still edit the repo directly), `depends_on` at run time, config precedence.

## Cross-Cutting Concerns
- Stack: bash + argc, tests in bats, tools managed via mise (`latest`, not pinned) (argc, jq, yq, bats); Arch container (`mise run test:container`) and PKGBUILD in `packaging/arch/`
- Intended architecture: skogai-runner will provide the single entrypoint for skogai 3.0 init/setup/bootstrap/install. `src/core/` holds system-level modules (think /etc/skogai, /usr/share/skogai); `.skogai/` is userspace / local override. argc is the interface for both user and agents.
- Key constraints: lowercase single-segment names; no sed/awk in the core template; trust existing tools (pacman, git, mise) instead of reinventing.

## Domain: core runner

### Decisions
- bash + argc chosen: argc gives one declarative CLI surface (help, completion, parsing) usable by humans and agents alike (2026-10-29)
- `best-version-so-far/` contains active module plans and reusable implementation. Foundation work comes first; tasks may reuse it deliberately. `agents/` and `docs/argc*` also contain reference material. Earlier validation claims need rechecking (clarified 2026-10-29)

- F001 is the relationship contract checker only (spec-gated 2026-10-30). Invalid input is a verdict (JSONL on stdout, exit 0); exit 2 bad args, exit 1 missing yq/jq. Old proposals (split main.sh, .skogai override, single binary) deferred per docs/plan.md (2026-10-30)
- Open plan-step-1 items, not yet features: operation identity / retry / linked intent revisions; configuration ownership and precedence (mise vs git config vs env vs module defaults). Step 2 writable-scope enforcement decided by skogix (2026-11-06): Podman, staged output. The command runs in Podman with the repo mounted read-only (as `mise run test:container` does) plus one empty writable output dir; the runner then verifies the output dir holds only paths in `owns` and only then moves them into place atomically. Out-of-scope writes are impossible inside the container (ro mount) and out-of-scope outputs are rejected before any effect. Implemented as F002 (2026-11-06): src/core/run/argc.sh check|run, example examples/hello.
- usage twins (2026-11-06): to compare argc with usage + mise, every argc piece has a usage twin with the same behavior and tests: `contract/usage.sh`, `run/usage.sh` (+ `examples/usage/hello`, `tests/fixtures/run-usage`), and `main-usage.sh` (`skogai`: no template/sync, usage `mount` reads the registry live; `SKOGAI_COMMANDS` is a `:`-list of registry layers, nearest first). Not spec-gated features; no entry in features.json. Until the comparison is decided, a change to a rule, runner, example or fixture goes into both twins. Open for skogix: criteria and decision for argc vs usage, and whether packaging (PKGBUILD) ships `skogai`.

- usage + mise chosen over argc as the interface for user, agents and modules (skogix, 2026-11-06). New work goes into the usage files only; the argc files are frozen, not removed. Why: one interface instead of twinning every change; usage gives layered registries (`SKOGAI_COMMANDS`), `effect=` for agents via `usage mcp`, and mise integration.
- Module model and config answers (skogix, 2026-11-07). `best-version-so-far/` is the reference target (config fold, module env, install by copy); it is deleted once everything is converted.
  - A module is three things: key/value config defaults, a usage declaration (strictly typed input -> output), and relationships. Candidate shape: one mise file, e.g. `mise.<name>.toml` (format not settled).
  - Relationships: `owns` = creates and is responsible for; `writes` = edits, i.e. gives input to the owning module to react to or use; `watches` = on an event at x, hand the event to executable y.
  - The entrypoint runs a module from anywhere (e.g. local). Once its tests and rules pass, it is copied to global (`~/.config/skogai`) or system (`/etc/skogai`).
  - Precedence, later wins: module defaults, system, global, local, override, command parameters, env. Plain Unix CLI practice.
  - Types are deferred; later modules validate paths, ints and so on.
  - Key/env names: kebab-case. `-` is part of a word and dropped in env; `.` maps to `_`, so `a.b-c.d` = `SKOGAI_A_BC_D` and `SKOGAI_FOO_BAR` = `skogai.foo.bar`.
  - Each module defines its own env, injected when it runs (mise does this for tasks).
  - `depends_on` at run time = the called command is available, i.e. that module is installed.
  - Workorder paths are relative to the git root.
- Verified in mise 2026.10.17 (scratch, 2026-11-07): a task's `usage` field validates args (a missing `<who>` is refused); `MISE_ENV=<name>` loads `mise.<name>.toml`; `[_.skogai]` free-form keys are readable with `mise config get`; `mise.local.toml` overrides it. A plain `[env]` value beats the caller's env. `"{{ get_env(name='X', default='d') }}"` lets the caller's env win, which the precedence above needs.
- mise conf.d (verified 2026-11-07, scratch): mise loads every `conf.d/*.toml` at each level: `/etc/mise/conf.d` (system; this host already has omarchy files there), `~/.config/mise/conf.d` (global, follows `MISE_CONFIG_DIR`), and the project's `.config/mise/conf.d` or `.mise/conf.d`. Tasks in a conf.d file run. `MISE_OVERRIDE_CONFIG_FILENAMES=skogai.toml` also works but is not needed. Proposal under discussion: a module's toml is a conf.d drop-in, and installing a module = copying it into the conf.d of the chosen level. Module entry docs (skogix): `SKOGAI.md` rather than AGENTS/CLAUDE/GEMINI/CODEX.md, plus MODULE.md or README.md for the module (not settled). `watches` is deferred.

# Context Summary

Persistent record of architectural decisions, discovered patterns, gotchas, and active context.
This file is referenced in CLAUDE.md and loaded every session.

## Active Context
- Steps 1-2 done (F001 checker, F002 staged Podman run). usage + mise is the interface; argc twins frozen (2026-11-06).
- Landed 2026-11-06: run events (`docs/evidence.md`), live-test examples (`tests/examples.bats`), `mise run test` on usage. Next: a second module that `depends_on` hello; step 3 leftovers (recovery, reader, workorder link).
- Not implemented: the workorder lifecycle through the runner (agents still edit the repo directly), `depends_on` at run time, config precedence.

## Cross-Cutting Concerns
- Stack: bash + argc, tests in bats, tools managed via mise (`latest`, not pinned) (argc, jq, yq, bats); Arch container (`mise run test:container`) and PKGBUILD in `packaging/arch/`
- Intended architecture: skogai-runner will provide the single entrypoint for skogai 3.0 init/setup/bootstrap/install. `src/core/` holds system-level modules (think /etc/skogai, /usr/share/skogai); `.skogai/` is userspace / local override. argc is the interface for both user and agents.
- Key constraints: lowercase single-segment names; no sed/awk in the core template; trust existing tools (pacman, git, mise) instead of reinventing.

## Domain: core runner

### Decisions
- bash + argc chosen: argc gives one declarative CLI surface (help, completion, parsing) usable by humans and agents alike (2026-10-29)
- `best-version-so-far/` contains active module plans and reusable implementation. Foundation work comes first; tasks may reuse it deliberately. `agents/` and `docs/argc*` also contain reference material. Earlier validation claims need rechecking (clarified 2026-10-29)

- F001 is the relationship contract checker only (spec-gated 2026-10-30). Invalid input is a verdict (JSONL on stdout, exit 0); exit 2 bad args, exit 1 missing yq/jq. Old proposals (split main.sh, .skogai override, single binary) deferred per docs/plan.md (2026-10-30)
- Open plan-step-1 items, not yet features: operation identity / retry / linked intent revisions; configuration ownership and precedence (mise vs git config vs env vs module defaults). Step 2 writable-scope enforcement decided by skogix (2026-11-06): Podman, staged output. The command runs in Podman with the repo mounted read-only (as `mise run test:container` does) plus one empty writable output dir; the runner then verifies the output dir holds only paths in `owns` and only then moves them into place atomically. Out-of-scope writes are impossible inside the container (ro mount) and out-of-scope outputs are rejected before any effect. Implemented as F002 (2026-11-06): src/core/run/argc.sh check|run, example examples/hello.
- usage twins (2026-11-06): to compare argc with usage + mise, every argc piece has a usage twin with the same behavior and tests: `contract/usage.sh`, `run/usage.sh` (+ `examples/usage/hello`, `tests/fixtures/run-usage`), and `main-usage.sh` (`skogai`: no template/sync, usage `mount` reads the registry live; `SKOGAI_COMMANDS` is a `:`-list of registry layers, nearest first). Not spec-gated features; no entry in features.json. Until the comparison is decided, a change to a rule, runner, example or fixture goes into both twins. Open for skogix: criteria and decision for argc vs usage, and whether packaging (PKGBUILD) ships `skogai`.

- usage + mise chosen over argc as the interface for user, agents and modules (skogix, 2026-11-06). New work goes into the usage files only; the argc files are frozen, not removed. Why: one interface instead of twinning every change; usage gives layered registries (`SKOGAI_COMMANDS`), `effect=` for agents via `usage mcp`, and mise integration.
- Module model and config answers (skogix, 2026-11-07). `best-version-so-far/` is the reference target (config fold, module env, install by copy); it is deleted once everything is converted.
  - A module is three things: key/value config defaults, a usage declaration (strictly typed input -> output), and relationships. Candidate shape: one mise file, e.g. `mise.<name>.toml` (format not settled).
  - Relationships: `owns` = creates and is responsible for; `writes` = edits, i.e. gives input to the owning module to react to or use; `watches` = on an event at x, hand the event to executable y.
  - The entrypoint runs a module from anywhere (e.g. local). Once its tests and rules pass, it is copied to global (`~/.config/skogai`) or system (`/etc/skogai`).
  - Precedence, later wins: module defaults, system, global, local, override, command parameters, env. Plain Unix CLI practice.
  - Types are deferred; later modules validate paths, ints and so on.
  - Key/env names: kebab-case. `-` is part of a word and dropped in env; `.` maps to `_`, so `a.b-c.d` = `SKOGAI_A_BC_D` and `SKOGAI_FOO_BAR` = `skogai.foo.bar`.
  - Each module defines its own env, injected when it runs (mise does this for tasks).
  - `depends_on` at run time = the called command is available, i.e. that module is installed.
  - Workorder paths are relative to the git root.
- Verified in mise 2026.10.17 (scratch, 2026-11-07): a task's `usage` field validates args (a missing `<who>` is refused); `MISE_ENV=<name>` loads `mise.<name>.toml`; `[_.skogai]` free-form keys are readable with `mise config get`; `mise.local.toml` overrides it. A plain `[env]` value beats the caller's env. `"{{ get_env(name='X', default='d') }}"` lets the caller's env win, which the precedence above needs.
- mise conf.d (verified 2026-11-07, scratch): mise loads every `conf.d/*.toml` at each level: `/etc/mise/conf.d` (system; this host already has omarchy files there), `~/.config/mise/conf.d` (global, follows `MISE_CONFIG_DIR`), and the project's `.config/mise/conf.d` or `.mise/conf.d`. Tasks in a conf.d file run. `MISE_OVERRIDE_CONFIG_FILENAMES=skogai.toml` also works but is not needed. Proposal under discussion: a module's toml is a conf.d drop-in, and installing a module = copying it into the conf.d of the chosen level. Module entry docs (skogix): `SKOGAI.md` rather than AGENTS/CLAUDE/GEMINI/CODEX.md, plus MODULE.md or README.md for the module (not settled). `watches` is deferred.
- Evidence starts from the skogai-core hook log shape (`/home/skogix/skogai/.skogai/logs/skogai-core/log.jsonl`: `{ts, event, action?, input}`), extended with run identity and outcome, not a new format (2026-11-06).

### Patterns
- Tests isolate HOME under `$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR` and drive the template via `argc --argc-run`.

### Gotchas
- Rootless podman finds its images through XDG_DATA_HOME (default $HOME/.local/share). Tests that isolate HOME must capture and export XDG_DATA_HOME first, or `podman image exists` fails. This host exports XDG_DATA_HOME already, which hides the problem.
- Do not add `:Z` to podman mounts of module dirs: SELinux relabelling changes the host directory, which is an effect outside `owns`.
- The runner logs to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/skogai/run.jsonl`. This host exports XDG_STATE_HOME, so isolating HOME alone leaks test runs into the real log: tests must set XDG_STATE_HOME and unset SKOGAI_LOG.
- A script reached through a registry symlink must `realpath` `BASH_SOURCE` before locating siblings (fixed in run/usage.sh, 9e82212). The tests copy `examples/usage/hello` whole, so a gitignored `greeting.txt` from a real run breaks 8 tests.
- Never write a file from `jq ... > file` in the Bash tool: a hook rewrites `jq` (even `/usr/bin/jq`) to `rtk jq`, which shortens long strings with `...`. This corrupted features.json once (2026-11-07, restored from git). Put the jq call in a script file and run `bash script.sh`.
- Workorder agents in worktrees under ~/skogai-runner/.claude/worktrees: a hook refuses plain `git` (rtk wrapper); they used `/usr/bin/git`. `mise tasks` there also picks up the parent checkout's mise.toml.
- `mise run test` stays on argc for the twinned files; `mise run test:usage` runs contract.bats and run.bats with `CONTRACT_IMPL=usage RUN_IMPL=usage` plus main-usage.bats. Both suites must pass after a twinned change.
- `contract/usage.sh` receives the variadic `file` as one shell-quoted string (`eval "files=(...)"`); under a usage mount, `usage_cmd` is the mounted script's `bin`, so main-usage.sh dispatches on argv.
- `mise run test` now depends on `mise run image` (cached `podman build`, a no-op without podman).
- No coverage tooling for bash/bats yet: the 95% coverage gate cannot be measured. `full_test` runs `bats tests` only. Enabling coverage (e.g. bashcov/kcov) needs its own feature if wanted.
- `ssh -T git@github.com` fails (no key loaded); remote is HTTPS under `skogai2`. The identity hook checks name/email only.
