#!/usr/bin/env -S usage bash
#USAGE bin "module"
#USAGE about "install modules into the mise conf.d of a level by copying, and list them"
#USAGE long_about """
#USAGE a module is a mise config file (<name>.toml, see docs/module.md). `install` runs the contract checker over the module together with everything already installed at the target level and the broader ones, runs the module's bats tests when it is a directory with a tests/ subdirectory, and only then copies the toml into the conf.d of the level: system (${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}/conf.d), global (the default, ${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.config/mise}/conf.d) or local (<git root>/.mise/conf.d). see docs/install.md.
#USAGE
#USAGE stdout is JSON lines. exit 0 done (including unchanged and absent), 1 a command line that does not fit the spec (usage's own), 2 bad arguments, path or name, a conflicting target file, the local level outside a git work tree, a checker failure or a missing tool, 3 rejected, 4 the effect failed.
#USAGE """
#USAGE cmd "install" effect="write" help="validate a module, then copy its toml into a level's conf.d" {
#USAGE   flag "--level <level>" default="global" help="where to install" { choices "system" "global" "local" }
#USAGE   arg "<path>" help="a module toml file, or a directory <d> holding <d>.toml (and optionally tests/)"
#USAGE }
#USAGE cmd "uninstall" effect="write" help="remove an installed module's toml from a level's conf.d" {
#USAGE   flag "--level <level>" default="global" help="where to remove from" { choices "system" "global" "local" }
#USAGE   arg "<name>" help="the module's name"
#USAGE }
#USAGE cmd "ls" effect="read" help="list the installed module files, system first, local last"
#
# usage parses the comments above and exports usage_cmd, usage_level, usage_path
# and usage_name. usage itself exits 1 when the command line does not fit the
# spec and 181 when the spec is broken.

# shellcheck shell=bash disable=SC2154 # usage_* are exported by usage
set -euo pipefail
# file lists are enumerated by glob: C-locale order everywhere
export LC_COLLATE=C

# resolve the symlink first: registered with skogai, BASH_SOURCE is the registry link
CONTRACT="$(cd "$(dirname "$(command realpath -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")/../contract" && pwd)/usage.sh"
LEVELS=(system global local)
NAME_RE='^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$'
GITROOT=""
STAGE=""
SC_LEVEL=() SC_PATH=() SC_NAME=() SC_DEPS=()

_err() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }

_ready() {
    local tool version
    for tool in git yq jq; do
        command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || { _err "missing tool: $tool"; return 2; }
    done
    # another program named yq would turn every file into "not a module"
    version="$(command yq --version 2>&1)" || true
    [[ "$version" == *mikefarah* ]] || { _err "wrong yq: need mikefarah/yq, found: ${version%%$'\n'*}"; return 2; }
    GITROOT="$(command git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || GITROOT=""
}

# the conf.d directories of a level, in mise's load order; local is empty outside git
_dirs() {
    case "$1" in
    system) printf '%s\n' "${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}/conf.d" ;;
    global) printf '%s\n' "${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mise}/conf.d" ;;
    local) [[ -z "$GITROOT" ]] || printf '%s\n%s\n' "$GITROOT/.mise/conf.d" "$GITROOT/.config/mise/conf.d" ;;
    esac
}

_index() {
    local i
    for i in "${!LEVELS[@]}"; do
        [[ "${LEVELS[i]}" != "$1" ]] || { printf '%s' "$i"; return; }
    done
}

# a skogai module file: parses as toml and _.skogai is a table with exactly one key
# whose value is a table. prints the name, then the depends_on strings as a JSON
# array; prints nothing for any other file
_info() {
    local doc
    doc="$(command yq -p toml -o json -I0 '.' "$1" 2>/dev/null)" || return 0
    command jq -r '
        if type == "object" and (._ | type) == "object" and (._.skogai | type) == "object"
           and (._.skogai | length) == 1 and (._.skogai | to_entries[0].value | type) == "object"
        then ._.skogai | to_entries[0]
             | .key, ([.value.depends_on? // [] | if type == "array" then .[] | select(type == "string") else empty end] | tojson)
        else empty end' <<<"$doc" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# every installed module file, levels in order, directories in order, names C-sorted
_scan() {
    SC_LEVEL=() SC_PATH=() SC_NAME=() SC_DEPS=()
    local level dir f info name deps
    for level in "${LEVELS[@]}"; do
        while IFS= read -r dir; do
            [[ -d "$dir" ]] || continue
            for f in "$dir"/*.toml; do
                [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
                info="$(_info "$f")"
                [[ -n "$info" ]] || continue
                { IFS= read -r name; IFS= read -r deps; } <<<"$info"
                SC_LEVEL+=("$level") SC_PATH+=("$f") SC_NAME+=("$name") SC_DEPS+=("$deps")
            done
        done < <(_dirs "$level")
    done
}

_line() { # module level path action
    command jq -cn --arg m "$1" --arg l "$2" --arg p "$3" --arg a "$4" \
        '{module: $m, level: $l, path: (if $p == "" then null else $p end), action: $a}'
}

_rejected() { # module level reasons-json
    command jq -cn --arg m "$1" --arg l "$2" --argjson r "$3" \
        '{module: (if $m == "" then null else $m end), level: $l, path: null, action: "rejected", reasons: $r}'
}

# target conf.d: the first directory of the level
_target_dir() {
    local dirs
    mapfile -t dirs < <(_dirs "$1")
    ((${#dirs[@]})) || { _err "the local level needs a git work tree"; return 2; }
    printf '%s' "${dirs[0]}"
}

install() {
    local level="$usage_level" path="$usage_path" src src_dir="" base name="" info tdir ti i files f out verdict reasons
    local action=installed target tname tmp
    _ready || return 2
    if [[ -d "$path" ]]; then
        src_dir="$(cd "$path" && pwd)"
        src="$src_dir/${src_dir##*/}.toml"
        [[ -f "$src" ]] || { _err "no ${src_dir##*/}.toml in $path"; return 2; }
    elif [[ -f "$path" && "${path##*/}" == ?*.toml ]]; then
        src="$path"
    else
        _err "not a module toml file or a module directory: $path"
        return 2
    fi
    base="${src##*/}"
    [[ "$base" != [-.]* ]] || { _err "unusable file name: $base"; return 2; }
    tdir="$(_target_dir "$level")" || return 2
    ti="$(_index "$level")"
    if [[ -n "$src_dir" ]] && compgen -G "$src_dir/tests/*.bats" >/dev/null; then
        command -v bats >/dev/null || { _err "missing tool: bats"; return 2; }
    fi
    info="$(_info "$src")"
    [[ -z "$info" ]] || IFS= read -r name <<<"$info"

    # 1. rules: the module among the installed ones, in one checker call
    _scan
    STAGE="$(command mktemp -d)"
    trap 'command rm -rf -- "$STAGE"' EXIT
    for i in "${!SC_PATH[@]}"; do
        (($(_index "${SC_LEVEL[i]}") <= ti)) || continue
        # the file this install would replace takes no part in the rules
        [[ -n "$name" && "$name" =~ $NAME_RE && "${SC_PATH[i]}" == "$tdir/$name.toml" ]] && continue
        command cp -- "${SC_PATH[i]}" "$STAGE/${SC_PATH[i]##*/}"
    done
    command cp -- "$src" "$STAGE/$base"
    files=()
    for f in "$STAGE"/*.toml; do files+=("${f##*/}"); done
    out="$(cd "$STAGE" && "$CONTRACT" check "${files[@]}")" || { _err "the contract checker failed"; return 2; }
    [[ "$(command jq -s 'length' <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null)" == "${#files[@]}" ]] ||
        { _err "unexpected output from the contract checker"; return 2; }
    verdict="$(command jq -r --arg f "$base" 'select(.file == $f) | .verdict' <<<"$out")"
    reasons="$(command jq -c --arg f "$base" 'select(.file == $f) | .reasons' <<<"$out")"
    if [[ "$verdict" != valid ]]; then
        _rejected "$name" "$level" "$reasons"
        return 3
    fi
    # 1b. the same name anywhere else, narrower levels included
    for i in "${!SC_PATH[@]}"; do
        if [[ "${SC_NAME[i]}" == "$name" && "${SC_PATH[i]}" != "$tdir/$name.toml" ]]; then
            _rejected "$name" "$level" '["duplicate-name"]'
            return 3
        fi
    done
    # 2. tests
    if [[ -n "$src_dir" ]] && compgen -G "$src_dir/tests/*.bats" >/dev/null; then
        (cd "$src_dir" && command bats "$src_dir/tests") >&2 || {
            _rejected "$name" "$level" '["tests-failed"]'
            return 3
        }
    fi
    # 3. target
    target="$tdir/$name.toml"
    if [[ -e "$target" || -L "$target" ]]; then
        info="$(_info "$target")"
        tname=""
        [[ -z "$info" ]] || IFS= read -r tname <<<"$info"
        [[ "$tname" == "$name" ]] || { _err "$target exists and is not the module $name"; return 2; }
        if command cmp -s -- "$src" "$target"; then
            _line "$name" "$level" "$target" unchanged
            return 0
        fi
        action=updated
    fi
    command mkdir -p -- "$tdir" || { _err "cannot create $tdir"; return 4; }
    # a name mise does not load, so a half-written file is never read
    tmp="$(command mktemp "$tdir/.install-XXXXXX")" || { _err "cannot write in $tdir"; return 4; }
    command cat -- "$src" >"$tmp" && command chmod 0644 -- "$tmp" && command mv -T -- "$tmp" "$target" || {
        command rm -f -- "$tmp"
        _err "cannot install $target"
        return 4
    }
    _line "$name" "$level" "$target" "$action"
}

uninstall() {
    local level="$usage_level" name="$usage_name" tdir target info tname="" i by=() required
    _ready || return 2
    [[ "$name" =~ $NAME_RE ]] || { _err "bad module name: $name"; return 2; }
    tdir="$(_target_dir "$level")" || return 2
    target="$tdir/$name.toml"
    if [[ ! -e "$target" && ! -L "$target" ]]; then
        _line "$name" "$level" "" absent
        return 0
    fi
    info="$(_info "$target")"
    [[ -z "$info" ]] || IFS= read -r tname <<<"$info"
    [[ "$tname" == "$name" ]] || { _err "$target is not the module $name"; return 2; }
    _scan
    for i in "${!SC_PATH[@]}"; do
        [[ "${SC_PATH[i]}" != "$target" ]] || continue
        [[ "$(command jq -r --arg n "$name" 'index($n) != null' <<<"${SC_DEPS[i]}")" == true ]] && by+=("${SC_NAME[i]}")
    done
    if ((${#by[@]})); then
        required="$(printf '%s\n' "${by[@]}" | command jq -Rcs 'split("\n") | map(select(. != "")) | unique')"
        command jq -cn --arg m "$name" --arg l "$level" --argjson r "$required" \
            '{module: $m, level: $l, path: null, action: "rejected", reasons: ["required-by"], required_by: $r}'
        return 3
    fi
    command rm -f -- "$target" || { _err "cannot remove $target"; return 4; }
    _line "$name" "$level" "$target" removed
}

ls() {
    local i
    _ready || return 2
    _scan
    for i in "${!SC_PATH[@]}"; do

"description": "Config over mise layers: `skogai config get|set|unset|list|files` reads and writes SKOGAI_* settings that live in mise's own [env] tables, so a value the user sets is the value the module's mise task sees. Usage port of best-version-so-far's `config` (modules/core/argc.sh), with mise files instead of git-config files (settled with skogix 2026-11-07, see context_summary "Module model and config answers").

Precedence, later wins (skogix's order): module default, system, global, local, override, caller env. Command parameters are the task's own usage args and are out of scope here. Mapping onto mise, verified by the lead on mise 2026.10.17 in an isolated sandbox on 2026-11-07 (to be re-proved by this feature's tests):
- module default: an [env] entry in a module toml (F003) in any conf.d, written `K = "{{ env.K | default(value='d') }}"`. `env.K` sees the caller env and every earlier layer, so a module installed in a later layer (e.g. project .mise/conf.d) still loses to system and global settings.
- system: `$SYS/config.toml`, SYS = ${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}.
- global: `$CFG/config.toml`, CFG = ${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mise}.
- local: `<git root>/mise.toml`, git root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the current directory.
- override: `<git root>/mise.local.toml`.
- caller env: wins over every layer because `config set` stores each value as `K = "{{ get_env(name='K', default='<value>') }}"` (a plain [env] value would beat the caller env; a get_env value does not).

Module files: a "skogai module file" is a `*.toml` in one of the conf.d directories below that yq parses and whose `_.skogai` is a table with exactly one key whose value is a table; that key is its name (the same definition as F005). Every other file there is ignored. The conf.d directories, in mise's load order (broadest first): `$SYS/conf.d`, `$CFG/conf.d`, `<git root>/.mise/conf.d`, `<git root>/.config/mise/conf.d`; files within one directory in C-locale order. Outside a git work tree the two project directories are not read.

Keys: a key is one or more `.`-separated segments, each matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$. Its env name is `SKOGAI_` + the key uppercased with `-` removed and `.` replaced by `_`: `hello.greeting` = SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING, `a.b-c.d` = SKOGAI_A_BC_D. The reverse (for list) is: drop `SKOGAI_`, lowercase, `_` becomes `.` (so dashes do not survive the round trip; documented). Any other key is exit 2.

Commands (new file src/core/config/usage.sh: a `usage bash` script with #USAGE specs and `case "$usage_cmd"` dispatch like src/core/contract/usage.sh; it must also work when reached through a registry symlink, `skogai register src/core/config/usage.sh config`):
- `get [--show-origin] <key>`: prints the resolved value and a newline, exit 0. Resolved value = the key's value in `mise env --json` run from the current directory; if mise does not define it but the caller env has it, the caller env value; else exit 3 with nothing on stdout. With --show-origin prints `<origin>\t<value>`. Origin: `env` when the caller env has the variable and its value equals the resolved one; else the highest-precedence file among override, local, global, system whose [env] table has the variable (printed as `override`, `local`, `global`, `system`); else the first module file in load order (broadest first, as above: with the env.K default form the earliest-loaded default wins) whose [env] has it, printed `module:<name>`; else `mise`. Origin is skogai's ladder, not mise's internal record: a value supplied by a file outside the ladder (a subdirectory mise.toml, `.mise.toml`, `.config/mise.toml`, config.override.toml, a module default not in the env.K form) can be attributed to a ladder file that also defines it. That is a documented known limit.
- `list [--show-origin]`: one `key=value` line per SKOGAI_* variable (name matching ^SKOGAI_[A-Z0-9_]+$) in `mise env --json` whose reverse key is a valid key (others, e.g. SKOGAI_A__B, are skipped), sorted by key (C locale); with --show-origin each line is `<origin>\t<key>=<value>`. Nothing defined: no output, exit 0. In list output and in `get --show-origin` output, a value is printed with `\` as `\\`, newline as `\n` and tab as `\t`; plain `get` prints the raw value.
- `set [--system|--global|--override] <key> <value>`: writes the get_env form into the chosen file (default local; at most one level flag, else exit 2), creating the file and its directory if missing, replacing an existing entry for that variable. Values containing `'`, `"`, `\`, any control character (newline, tab, CR, ...), or any of `{{ }} {% %} {# #}` are refused with exit 2 and the file is untouched. The empty value is allowed. An existing target file that yq cannot parse as TOML: exit 2, untouched. The write is atomic: copy the target (or an empty file) to a temporary file in the same directory whose name mise does not load (e.g. `.skogai-set-XXXXXX.toml`), edit that copy (preferably with `mise set --file` / `mise unset --file`, trusting mise's TOML editing), then rename it over the target; on failure the temporary file is removed and the target untouched, exit 2. Contract tested on the standard form (`K = "..."` lines under an `[env]` header): every other line (comments, other tables, other [env] keys) is kept, and a second set leaves one entry. For other forms (inline `env = {...}`, dotted `env.K`, duplicates) the outcome is whatever the mise edit does, provided `mise env` then resolves the new value; docs say so.
- `unset [--system|--global|--override] <key>`: removes the variable from that file's [env], same atomic write; absent variable or absent file is exit 0 with no change (idempotent). Other content kept as for set.
- `files`: one `<layer>\t<path>\t<present|missing>` line for system, global, local, override in that order, then one `module:<name>\t<path>\tpresent` line per module file in load order (see Module files). Outside a git work tree the local and override lines print `-` as the path and `missing`, and no project module lines are printed.
Outside a git work tree, set/unset without --system/--global exit 2. A failing mise call (e.g. an untrusted config) exits 2 with mise's stderr passed through. Missing git, mise, jq or yq: exit 2 with a message. Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 only from usage's own parser (missing <key>, unknown flag; contract/usage.sh records this); 2 bad args, refused value, tool or mise failure; 3 get of an undefined key. Diagnostics go to stderr only.

Module defaults: change examples/modules/hello/hello.toml to `SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING = "{{ env.SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING | default(value='hi') }}"` and say in docs/module.md that module defaults use this form and why (a get_env default in a later layer beats earlier settings). The checker does not enforce the form in this feature. tests/module.bats must stay green unchanged (its live test still prints `hi world` / `yo world`).

Docs: new docs/config.md: the layers and files, the key mapping, the stored form, every command with output and exit codes, marked implemented/verified, and the known limits: the reverse mapping loses `-`; a shell with `mise activate` exports resolved SKOGAI_* values, so they show as origin `env`; values with the refused characters cannot be stored (types are deferred).

Evidence (QA binding): evidence_type unit + integration. tests/config.bats. Every test isolates mise like tests/module.bats: `env -i PATH HOME` plus MISE_CONFIG_DIR, MISE_SYSTEM_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR, MISE_STATE_DIR, MISE_CACHE_DIR, MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR, XDG_STATE_HOME isolated, and a `git init` project dir. Required cases:
1. Precedence ladder: hello.toml copied into the project's .mise/conf.d; then step by step: nothing set -> `get --show-origin hello.greeting` = `module:hello\thi`; `set --system` sys -> system; `set --global` glob -> global; `set` loc -> local; `set --override` ovr -> override; caller env SKOGAI_HELLO_GREETING=env -> `env`. At every step `mise run -q hello world` from the project prints `<that value> world` (the task sees what get reports).
2. A global setting beats a module installed in the project conf.d (the env.K default form).
3. set keeps a comment and a [tools] table already in mise.toml; set twice leaves one entry; unset removes it and a second unset is exit 0.
4. Refused values (each of the listed characters, plus a tab) exit 2 and leave the file byte-identical; an unparseable mise.toml makes set exit 2 and stays byte-identical; no `.skogai-set-*` file is left behind in any case.
5. Invalid keys (`Hello`, `a..b`, `.a`, `a.`, `1a`, empty) exit 2.
6. get of an unset key: exit 3, empty stdout.
7. list output exact for a known setup, with and without --show-origin, including a variable whose reverse key is invalid (skipped) and a hand-written value containing a tab (escaped).
8. files output exact inside a git dir and outside one, with a host-style non-module file in a conf.d (not listed).
9. Through the registry: `skogai register src/core/config/usage.sh config` into a temporary SKOGAI_COMMANDS (SKOGAI_MAIN pointing at src/core/main-usage.sh, as tests/main-usage.bats does), then `skogai config set --global hello.greeting x` exits 0 and `skogai config get --show-origin hello.greeting` prints exactly `global\tx`.

"description": "Module install by copy: `skogai module install|uninstall|ls` puts a module's toml (F003 format) into the mise conf.d of a level after its rules and tests pass, so mise then loads its [env], [tasks] and relationships for every project at that level (settled with skogix 2026-11-07: "point to any module from wherever ... if all tests/rules are followed they are copied to global or system level"; mise conf.d chosen as the storage, see context_summary "mise conf.d").

Levels and their conf.d directories:
- system: ${MISE_SYSTEM_DIR:-/etc/mise}/conf.d
- global (default): ${MISE_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mise}/conf.d
- local: install and uninstall write <git root>/.mise/conf.d; reading (ls, rules, the duplicate-name scan, required-by) covers both <git root>/.mise/conf.d and <git root>/.config/mise/conf.d (mise loads both), in that order. git root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the current directory. Outside a git work tree the local level is exit 2 for install/uninstall, and it is simply left out of ls, the rules set, the duplicate-name scan and required-by.
Paths (the JSON `path` field, the conf.d directories) are built literally from those variables and the git root, not passed through realpath.
Precedence order (broadest first) is system, global, local. A "skogai module file" in a conf.d is a `*.toml` that yq parses, whose `_.skogai` is a table with exactly one key whose value is a table; that key is the module's name. Every other file there (the host's own conf.d files, files with several `_.skogai` keys, unparseable files) is ignored by all three commands and never touched.

Commands (new file src/core/module/usage.sh: a `usage bash` script with #USAGE specs and `case "$usage_cmd"` dispatch like src/core/contract/usage.sh; it locates ../contract/usage.sh after resolving its own symlink with realpath, so it works through `skogai register src/core/module/usage.sh module`):

`install [--level system|global|local] <path>`: <path> is a module toml file, or a directory <d> holding <basename d>.toml (that file is the module; anything else is exit 2, nothing written). Steps, all before any effect:
1. Rules: copy into a fresh temporary directory T, flat, under their own file names: first the skogai module files installed at the target level and every broader level (broadest level first; a later file with the same file name replaces an earlier one), except the file <conf.d>/<name>.toml at the target level that this install would replace; then the source toml under its own file name (replacing any copy of the same file name). Run `contract/usage.sh check` on every *.toml in T in one call (C-locale sorted). The source's verdict must be `valid`. Consequences (each tested): an unparseable or invalid module is rejected with its reasons; a module whose depends_on names a module not installed at the target or a broader level is rejected (missing-dependency); two modules owning the same path are rejected (ownership-conflict, paths relative to the conf.d as all files sit in T).
1b. Duplicate name at any level: if the source is valid, and a skogai module file declaring the same name is installed at any level (narrower ones included) other than the target file <conf.d>/<name>.toml itself, the install is rejected with reason `duplicate-name`. This scan is separate from the checker so that narrower levels do not satisfy missing-dependency.
If contract/usage.sh exits non-zero or its output is not one JSON verdict per file, install exits 2 with its stderr passed through, nothing on stdout, nothing written.
2. Tests: if <path> is a directory with a tests/ subdirectory holding at least one *.bats file, `bats <d>/tests` runs with <d> as working directory and must exit 0, else rejected with reason `tests-failed`. A toml file path has no tests.
3. Target: <conf.d>/<name>.toml, name = the source's `_.skogai` key. If it exists and is not a skogai module file declaring that same name, exit 2 and nothing is written.
Effect: if the target exists with identical bytes, nothing is written (action `unchanged`). Otherwise the conf.d directory is created if needed, the source is copied to a temporary file in the same directory whose name does not end in `.toml` (so mise never loads a half-written file), and moved over the target in one rename (action `installed`, or `updated` when a target existed). Only the toml is copied (README.md, SKOGAI.md, tests/ stay in the source); docs/install.md says a module's task must therefore not depend on files beside its toml.
Output: one JSON line on stdout, `{"module": <name>, "level": <level>, "path": <absolute target path>, "action": "installed"|"updated"|"unchanged"}`, exit 0. Rejected: one JSON line `{"module": <name or null>, "level": <level>, "path": null, "action": "rejected", "reasons": [...]}` (the source's contract reasons sorted unique, or ["duplicate-name"], or ["tests-failed"]), exit 3, nothing written; the bats output goes to stderr. If creating the directory, copying or renaming fails (e.g. no permission at the system level): exit 4, a message on stderr, nothing on stdout, and the temporary file is removed.

`uninstall [--level system|global|local] <name>`: <name> must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$, else exit 2. Target <conf.d>/<name>.toml (for local: <git root>/.mise/conf.d only). Absent: `{"module", "level", "path": null, "action": "absent"}` exit 0. Present but not a skogai module file declaring <name>: exit 2, untouched. If any skogai module file installed at any level (other than the target itself) lists <name> in depends_on: rejected, `{"module", "level", "path": null, "action": "rejected", "reasons": ["required-by"], "required_by": [names, sorted]}` exit 3, untouched. Else the file is removed, `{"module", "level", "path", "action": "removed"}` exit 0. If removing fails: exit 4, message on stderr, nothing on stdout.

`ls`: one JSON line `{"module", "level", "path"}` per skogai module file, levels in order system, global, local; within a level directory by directory in the order given above (local: .mise/conf.d, then .config/mise/conf.d), files C-locale sorted by file name within each directory. The same order is used wherever installed files are enumerated (T, the duplicate-name scan, required-by). No modules: no output, exit 0.

Exit codes: 0 done (including unchanged/absent); 1 only from usage's own parser (a command line that does not fit the #USAGE spec, as in run/usage.sh); 2 bad args, bad path or name, target conflict, local level outside git, checker failure, or a missing tool (git, yq, jq, and bats when tests exist); 3 rejected; 4 the effect failed. Diagnostics on stderr only.

Docs: new docs/install.md: levels and directories, what counts as a module file, the checks and their order, the output and exit codes, marked implemented/verified, and the known limits: same-named modules at two levels are refused rather than shadowed; owns paths of installed modules are compared relative to their conf.d; module tests run unisolated in the module's directory.

Evidence (QA binding): evidence_type unit + integration. tests/install.bats with fixtures under tests/fixtures/install/ (module directories and toml files of its own; it must not modify examples/). Every test isolates HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME, MISE_SYSTEM_DIR, MISE_CONFIG_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR, MISE_STATE_DIR, MISE_CACHE_DIR and MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR and uses a `git init` project dir. Required cases: install to each level puts the file in the right conf.d and prints the exact JSON; a second install is `unchanged` with the file's mtime unchanged; a changed source gives `updated`; an invalid module (one F003 reason fixture) is rejected with that reason and nothing is written; missing-dependency rejected, then accepted after the dependency is installed at a broader level; duplicate-name rejected both when the same name sits at a broader level and at a narrower one (e.g. installed local, installing global); a missing-dependency is not satisfied by a module at a narrower level; uninstall of an invalid name (`../x`) exit 2; a module in <git root>/.config/mise/conf.d shows in ls as level local; a read-only conf.d directory gives exit 4 with no temporary file left; ownership-conflict with an installed module rejected; a module directory whose bats test fails is rejected with tests-failed, and one whose test passes is installed; a foreign non-module file at the target name gives exit 2 and is untouched; foreign files in conf.d are ignored by ls and by the rules; uninstall removes, then reports absent; uninstall refused while another installed module depends on it; local level outside a git dir is exit 2; live: after `install --level global` of a fixture module with a task, `mise run -q <task>` (isolated mise as in tests/module.bats, from the project dir) runs it, and after uninstall the task is gone (mise exits non-zero). # Context Summary

Persistent record of architectural decisions, discovered patterns, gotchas, and active context.
This file is referenced in CLAUDE.md and loaded every session.

## Active Context
- Steps 1-2 done (F001 checker, F002 staged Podman run). usage + mise is the interface; argc twins frozen (2026-11-06).
- Landed 2026-11-06: run events (`docs/evidence.md`), live-test examples (`tests/examples.bats`), `mise run test` on usage. Next: a second module that `depends_on` hello; step 3 leftovers (recovery, reader, workorder link).
- Not implemented: the workorder lifecycle through the runner (agents still edit the repo directly), `depends_on` at run time, config precedence.

## Cross-Cutting Concerns
- Stack: bash + argc, tests in bats, tools managed via mise (`latest`, not pinned) (argc, jq, yq, bats); Arch container (`mise run test:container`) and PKGBUILD in `packaging/arch/`
- Intended architecture: skogai-runner will provide the single entrypoint for skogai 3.0 init/setup/bootstrap/install. `src/core/` holds system-level modules (think /etc/skogai, /usr/share/skogai); `.skogai/` is userspace / local override. argc is the interface for both user and agents.
- Key constraints: lowercase single-segment names; no sed/awk in the core template; trust existing tools (pacman, git, mise) instead of reinventing.

## Domain: core runner

### Decisions
- bash + argc chosen: argc gives one declarative CLI surface (help, completion, parsing) usable by humans and agents alike (2026-10-29)
- `best-version-so-far/` contains active module plans and reusable implementation. Foundation work comes first; tasks may reuse it deliberately. `agents/` and `docs/argc*` also contain reference material. Earlier validation claims need rechecking (clarified 2026-10-29)

- F001 is the relationship contract checker only (spec-gated 2026-10-30). Invalid input is a verdict (JSONL on stdout, exit 0); exit 2 bad args, exit 1 missing yq/jq. Old proposals (split main.sh, .skogai override, single binary) deferred per docs/plan.md (2026-10-30)
- Open plan-step-1 items, not yet features: operation identity / retry / linked intent revisions; configuration ownership and precedence (mise vs git config vs env vs module defaults). Step 2 writable-scope enforcement decided by skogix (2026-11-06): Podman, staged output. The command runs in Podman with the repo mounted read-only (as `mise run test:container` does) plus one empty writable output dir; the runner then verifies the output dir holds only paths in `owns` and only then moves them into place atomically. Out-of-scope writes are impossible inside the container (ro mount) and out-of-scope outputs are rejected before any effect. Implemented as F002 (2026-11-06): src/core/run/argc.sh check|run, example examples/hello.
- usage twins (2026-11-06): to compare argc with usage + mise, every argc piece has a usage twin with the same behavior and tests: `contract/usage.sh`, `run/usage.sh` (+ `examples/usage/hello`, `tests/fixtures/run-usage`), and `main-usage.sh` (`skogai`: no template/sync, usage `mount` reads the registry live; `SKOGAI_COMMANDS` is a `:`-list of registry layers, nearest first). Not spec-gated features; no entry in features.json. Until the comparison is decided, a change to a rule, runner, example or fixture goes into both twins. Open for skogix: criteria and decision for argc vs usage, and whether packaging (PKGBUILD) ships `skogai`.

- usage + mise chosen over argc as the interface for user, agents and modules (skogix, 2026-11-06). New work goes into the usage files only; the argc files are frozen, not removed. Why: one interface instead of twinning every change; usage gives layered registries (`SKOGAI_COMMANDS`), `effect=` for agents via `usage mcp`, and mise integration.
- Module model and config answers (skogix, 2026-11-07). `best-version-so-far/` is the reference target (config fold, module env, install by copy); it is deleted once everything is converted.
  - A module is three things: key/value config defaults, a usage declaration (strictly typed input -> output), and relationships. Candidate shape: one mise file, e.g. `mise.<name>.toml` (format not settled).
  - Relationships: `owns` = creates and is responsible for; `writes` = edits, i.e. gives input to the owning module to react to or use; `watches` = on an event at x, hand the event to executable y.
  - The entrypoint runs a module from anywhere (e.g. local). Once its tests and rules pass, it is copied to global (`~/.config/skogai`) or system (`/etc/skogai`).
  - Precedence, later wins: module defaults, system, global, local, override, command parameters, env. Plain Unix CLI practice.
  - Types are deferred; later modules validate paths, ints and so on.
  - Key/env names: kebab-case. `-` is part of a word and dropped in env; `.` maps to `_`, so `a.b-c.d` = `SKOGAI_A_BC_D` and `SKOGAI_FOO_BAR` = `skogai.foo.bar`.
  - Each module defines its own env, injected when it runs (mise does this for tasks).
  - `depends_on` at run time = the called command is available, i.e. that module is installed.
  - Workorder paths are relative to the git root.
- Verified in mise 2026.10.17 (scratch, 2026-11-07): a task's `usage` field validates args (a missing `<who>` is refused); `MISE_ENV=<name>` loads `mise.<name>.toml`; `[_.skogai]` free-form keys are readable with `mise config get`; `mise.local.toml` overrides it. A plain `[env]` value beats the caller's env. `"{{ get_env(name='X', default='d') }}"` lets the caller's env win, which the precedence above needs.
- mise conf.d (verified 2026-11-07, scratch): mise loads every `conf.d/*.toml` at each level: `/etc/mise/conf.d` (system; this host already has omarchy files there), `~/.config/mise/conf.d` (global, follows `MISE_CONFIG_DIR`), and the project's `.config/mise/conf.d` or `.mise/conf.d`. Tasks in a conf.d file run. `MISE_OVERRIDE_CONFIG_FILENAMES=skogai.toml` also works but is not needed. Layer merge (same session): `[env]` merges key by key and the later layer wins; a later `[tasks.x]` replaces the whole task, so `run` and `usage` vanish silently; `mise config get _.x` reads only the nearest file. An empty .toml parses to `null` in yq. A test can isolate mise with `env -i` plus MISE_CONFIG_DIR, MISE_SYSTEM_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR, MISE_STATE_DIR, MISE_CACHE_DIR and MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS: then `/etc/mise/conf.d` is not loaded. Proposal under discussion: a module's toml is a conf.d drop-in, and installing a module = copying it into the conf.d of the chosen level. Module entry docs (skogix): `SKOGAI.md` rather than AGENTS/CLAUDE/GEMINI/CODEX.md, plus MODULE.md or README.md for the module (not settled). `watches` is deferred.
- Config layering on mise (verified 2026-11-07, scratch, mise 2026.10.17; basis of F004/F005): skogix's precedence maps onto mise as module default `K = "{{ env.K | default(value='d') }}"` in a conf.d (env.K sees the caller env and earlier layers, so a project-installed module still loses to system/global) < `$MISE_SYSTEM_DIR/config.toml` < `$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml` < `<git root>/mise.toml` < `mise.local.toml` (< `config.override.toml`, which `mise set --override` writes). Stored values written as `{{ get_env(name='K', default='v') }}` let the caller env win at every layer, inside tasks too; a plain value beats the caller env. `mise env --json` gives the resolved values. `mise set` (list) names the module file as source even when another layer supplied the value, so origin must be computed by skogai. Within one level conf.d files load before config.toml.
- Evidence starts from the skogai-core hook log shape (`/home/skogix/skogai/.skogai/logs/skogai-core/log.jsonl`: `{ts, event, action?, input}`), extended with run identity and outcome, not a new format (2026-11-06).

### Patterns
- Tests isolate HOME under `$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR` and drive the template via `argc --argc-run`.

### Gotchas
- Rootless podman finds its images through XDG_DATA_HOME (default $HOME/.local/share). Tests that isolate HOME must capture and export XDG_DATA_HOME first, or `podman image exists` fails. This host exports XDG_DATA_HOME already, which hides the problem.
- Do not add `:Z` to podman mounts of module dirs: SELinux relabelling changes the host directory, which is an effect outside `owns`.
- The runner logs to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/skogai/run.jsonl`. This host exports XDG_STATE_HOME, so isolating HOME alone leaks test runs into the real log: tests must set XDG_STATE_HOME and unset SKOGAI_LOG.
- A script reached through a registry symlink must `realpath` `BASH_SOURCE` before locating siblings (fixed in run/usage.sh, 9e82212). The tests copy `examples/usage/hello` whole, so a gitignored `greeting.txt` from a real run breaks 8 tests.
- Never write a file from `jq ... > file` in the Bash tool: a hook rewrites `jq` (even `/usr/bin/jq`) to `rtk jq`, which shortens long strings with `...`. This corrupted features.json once (2026-11-07, restored from git). Put the jq call in a script file and run `bash script.sh`.
- Workorder agents in worktrees under ~/skogai-runner/.claude/worktrees: a hook refuses plain `git` (rtk wrapper); they used `/usr/bin/git`. `mise tasks` there also picks up the parent checkout's mise.toml.
- `mise run test` stays on argc for the twinned files; `mise run test:usage` runs contract.bats and run.bats with `CONTRACT_IMPL=usage RUN_IMPL=usage` plus main-usage.bats. Both suites must pass after a twinned change.
- `contract/usage.sh` receives the variadic `file` as one shell-quoted string (`eval "files=(...)"`); under a usage mount, `usage_cmd` is the mounted script's `bin`, so main-usage.sh dispatches on argv.
- `mise run test` now depends on `mise run image` (cached `podman build`, a no-op without podman).
- No coverage tooling for bash/bats yet: the 95% coverage gate cannot be measured. `full_test` runs `bats tests` only. Enabling coverage (e.g. bashcov/kcov) needs its own feature if wanted.
- `ssh -T git@github.com` fails (no key loaded); remote is HTTPS under `skogai2`. The identity hook checks name/email only.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

- @.skogai/TODO.md contains one-line descriptions of tasks to be done
- !`wt step diff -- --cached > .skogai/tmp/wt-git-diff-cached` generates the file @.skogai/tmp/wt-git-diff-cached to show the users staged changes. see this as "proposed changes" or that it should actively be considered together with the users message.

Read @AGENTS.md (working principles) and `.harness/context_summary.md` (decisions, gotchas) at session start. `docs/design.md` and `docs/plan.md` hold the vision and the foundation-first sequence.

**Continuing work** goes through [.skogai/workorders/WORKORDERS.md](.skogai/workorders/WORKORDERS.md). In the lead session, check the queue there and hand out `open/` workorders to agents. If you were given a workorder, implement only that one, inside its `owns`.

## Commands

Tools come from `mise.toml` (argc, jq, yq, bats, all `latest`): `mise install`. Run checks through mise (`mise run test`, `mise exec -- bats ...`). The system `yq` may be a different program from mikefarah's yq, and then every contract test fails with `invalid-yaml`.

- `mise run test`: the whole Bats suite against the usage implementations (`CONTRACT_IMPL=usage RUN_IMPL=usage bats tests`)
- `mise run test:argc`: the frozen argc side (`tests/contract.bats`, `tests/run.bats` on `argc.sh`)
- `bats tests/main.bats` or `bats tests/contract.bats`: one file
- `bats -f '<regex>' tests/main.bats`: tests whose name matches
- `mise run test:container`: the same suite in a clean Arch container via Podman (the repo is mounted read-only at `/repo`)
- `.harness/init.sh smoke_test`: `bash -n` on tracked scripts, plus `shellcheck -S error` when installed. `best-version-so-far/` and `docs/` are excluded
- `.harness/init.sh focused_test <file>` / `full_test`: the harness's single-file and full runs

Run a script directly with `argc --argc-run <script> <cmd> ...`. From a checkout, point the runner at temporary paths so nothing touches real `~/Argcfile.sh` or `~/.config/argc/commands`:

```bash
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
export ARGC_COMMANDS="$tmp/commands" ARGC_MAIN="$tmp/Argcfile.sh" ARGC_TEMPLATE="$PWD/src/core/main.sh"
argc --argc-run "$ARGC_TEMPLATE" register <file> <name>
argc --argc-run "$ARGC_MAIN" --help
```

The README demo uses `scripts/memory.sh`, which is not in this checkout. Use any small argc script instead.

## Architecture

**usage is the interface going forward (skogix, 2026-11-06).** New work lands in the usage files (`main-usage.sh`, `contract/usage.sh`, `run/usage.sh`, `examples/usage/`, `tests/fixtures/run-usage/`). The argc files below stay as they are, frozen: they are not extended, and whether to remove them is undecided. The "goes into both" rules for the twins no longer apply to new features.

Everything is Bash, and argc comment tags (`# @cmd`, `# @arg`, `# @meta`, `# @env`) form the interface: they provide parsing, help, completion and JSON export (`argc --argc-export`). Each script ends with `eval "$(argc --argc-eval "$0" "$@")"`, and argc sets `argc_*` variables before the function runs.

**`src/core/main.sh`: the packaged runner.** It is a template, not the file users run. `sync` copies the template minus its final eval line, adds one generated recipe per symlink in the registry (`ARGC_COMMANDS/<name>.sh`), and puts the eval line back. It validates the result with `argc --argc-export`, then moves it over `ARGC_MAIN` in one step. Each generated recipe calls `_delegate`, which `cd`s to `ARGC_PWD` (the caller's directory, since argc runs from the Argcfile's directory) and runs `argc --argc-run` on the registered script. `_choice_delegate` sends completion to the child script's own `--argc-compgen`. Things to keep intact:
- `sync` requires the template's last line to be exactly the eval line, and tests check that the output has exactly one.
- The generated main is never edited by hand. Changes go in the template or in the registered scripts.
- Registered names become shell functions, so `_reserved` rejects runner commands, builtins and keywords. External tools are called as `command <tool>` so a registered name like `rm` cannot shadow them.
- The packaged default `ARGC_TEMPLATE=/usr/share/skogai/core/main.sh` comes from `packaging/arch/PKGBUILD`, which builds the **committed HEAD**.

**`src/core/contract/argc.sh`: the relationship contract checker (feature F001).** `check <file>...` reads Markdown+ frontmatter (the keys are `name`, `description`, `depends_on`, `reads`, `writes`, `owns`, `watches`, `defaults`) and prints one JSON verdict per file: `{file, verdict, reasons}`. Bash handles the parse stage (frontmatter → yq → JSON records). A single jq program (`VERDICTS`) applies the per-file and cross-file rules (missing-dependency, duplicate-name, ownership-conflict, write-not-owned, path-outside-scope, …). An invalid file still counts as an answer, so the exit code is 0. Exit 2 means bad arguments and exit 1 means yq or jq is missing.

**`src/core/contract/usage.sh`: the usage twin of `contract/argc.sh`.** Same rules (the jq program and frontmatter parse are copied verbatim), same output and exit codes; only the interface differs: `#USAGE` comments and a `usage bash` shebang instead of `# @cmd`/`# @arg` and `--argc-eval`, a `case "$usage_cmd"` instead of function dispatch, and the variadic `file` arrives as one shell-quoted string (`eval "files=(...)"`). It exists to compare argc with usage + mise. A rule change goes into both files.

**`src/core/run/usage.sh`: the usage twin of `run/argc.sh`.** Same checks, JSON and exit codes. Its modules are usage scripts: `usage lint` replaces `argc --argc-export` (so a module command without a usage spec is `invalid-command`), the container runs `usage bash /work/<name>.sh`, it calls `contract/usage.sh`, and the image can also be passed as `--image` (env `SKOGAI_IMAGE`). `check` declares `effect="read"` and `run` `effect="write"`, which `usage mcp -f src/core/run/usage.sh` reports to agents. The usage example is `examples/usage/hello/` and the usage fixtures are `tests/fixtures/run-usage/` (same `.md` files, commands rewritten for usage). A change to a runner, an example or a fixture goes into both.

**`src/core/main-usage.sh`: the usage twin of `main.sh`.** Invoked as `skogai`. No template, no `sync`, no generated main: `register` lints the script with `usage lint` and symlinks it into `SKOGAI_COMMANDS` (default `~/.config/skogai/commands`), and a top-level `mount` asks `"${SKOGAI_MAIN:-skogai}" _mount` for the registry whenever usage needs it (help, completion, or a word it doesn't know). `_mount` emits one `cmd` per name with a nested mount to `_spec <name>`, which prints that script's `#USAGE` lines (extracted the way usage itself reads them). Things to keep intact:
- Dispatch reads the registered name from argv, not `usage_cmd`: under a mount, `usage_cmd` is named after the mounted script's `bin`.
- `_delegate` unsets every `usage_*` before `exec usage bash <script>`, so the script parses its own arguments from scratch.
- `_mount` must never fail: a gone target is emitted as a hidden catch-all (so running it reaches the clear "is gone" error), and a script that no longer lints gets a catch-all spec (so it fails alone, by itself). Names don't become functions, so only `register unregister ls help` are reserved.
- `SKOGAI_COMMANDS` is a `:`-list of registry layers, nearest first (empty entries skipped, none at all is exit 2). Every lookup goes through `_resolve` (first layer with the name wins, gone links included), `_names` merges all layers, and `register`/`unregister` touch only the first layer. This replaces argc's "nearest Argcfile wins": a project puts its own layer in front, e.g. mise `[env] SKOGAI_COMMANDS = "{{config_root}}/.skogai/commands:{{env.HOME}}/.config/skogai/commands"`.
- From a checkout, set `SKOGAI_MAIN="$PWD/src/core/main-usage.sh"` and point `SKOGAI_COMMANDS` at a temp dir; tests do both (`tests/main-usage.bats`).

`mise run test` runs every suite with `CONTRACT_IMPL=usage RUN_IMPL=usage`; `mise run test:argc` runs `tests/contract.bats` and `tests/run.bats` against the frozen argc files.

**Run events.** `run/usage.sh` appends one JSONL event per `check`/`exec`/`apply`/`end` step to `--log` (env `SKOGAI_LOG`, default `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/skogai/run.jsonl`), in the skogai-core envelope `{ts, event, action?, input}` plus `id, run, module, revision, outcome`. See `docs/evidence.md`. Every test that calls the runner must isolate `XDG_STATE_HOME` and unset `SKOGAI_LOG`, or it writes to the real log.

`tests/examples.bats` turns every `examples/usage/<name>/<name>.md` into a live test (check valid; run applied; second run unchanged). A new example is a new test.

**Tests.** Each test sets `HOME` and every `ARGC_*` path under `$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR` and drives scripts through `argc --argc-run`. Contract fixtures follow a naming rule: each `tests/fixtures/contract/invalid/<reason>/` directory must produce exactly the reason `<reason>`. Each multi-file case directory under `valid/` (or `invalid/`) is checked as a single call, against its `expected.jsonl` where one exists. Add a new rule by adding a fixture directory named after its reason.

**`best-version-so-far/`** is the earlier module-based design (`bin/skogai`, `modules/`, `docs/module.md`, `HANDOVER.md`). It is still active, but `bats tests` doesn't run it, and its old validation claims need rechecking before reuse. `docs/argc/` and `docs/argc-completions/` are upstream reference snapshots of unknown revision, so check the pinned links in `docs/argc-guide.md` before relying on version-sensitive argc behavior.

## Conventions specific to this repo

- Machine-readable output goes to stdout and diagnostics to stderr. Validate before any effect, and make effects idempotent.
- Names are lowercase, one segment (`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`). Don't use sed or awk in the core template. Prefer existing tools (git, mise, pacman) over new machinery.
- Documentation must keep *intended*, *implemented* and *verified* behavior separate. Workorders, JSONL evidence and capability enforcement are planned and not implemented yet.

## Harness

This project uses the Long-Running Agent Harness (vv-harness plugin).

- Feature tracking: `.harness/features.json`
- Context and decisions: `.harness/context_summary.md`
- Progress handoff: `.harness/claude-progress.txt`

# Workorders

This folder is where to go next. The lead session (the orchestrator) keeps a queue of small, self-contained jobs. Each job goes to another agent, which implements it on its own branch and opens a draft PR. The lead keeps the plan and reviews the results. The agents only see what their workorder gives them.

These are hand-prepared workorders, not the [step 2 lifecycle](../../docs/plan.md). Nothing in this folder enforces capabilities or records evidence yet.

## Routes

- `open/*.md`: ready to hand out. Every file in this folder can run in parallel with the others.
- `done/*.md`: finished. The lead moves a workorder here in the same change that lands its PR.
- Next (`log-partial-line` and `log-reader` have landed): a `run-workorder-link` workorder, so events name the workorder and commit they belong to. It owns `src/core/run/usage.sh`.
- After that: a `hello-reader` example that `depends_on` hello and reads its `greeting.txt`. This needs `depends_on` to work at run time and settles the path-base question below, so it waits until then. The staged runner (`src/core/run/usage.sh`) still isn't used for handing out workorders: agents edit the repo directly.

## A workorder

A Markdown+ file. The frontmatter is what the [contract checker](../../src/core/contract/argc.sh) can verify. The body is the instruction.

- `name`: lowercase, one segment, unique. Also the branch and PR title suffix.
- `owns`: the only files the agent may create or change, relative to the repo root. Two open workorders must never own the same path. That is what makes handing them out in parallel safe. List individual files, never directories: the checker only flags identical paths, so `examples/` and `examples/demo.sh` would both pass.
- `reads`: what the agent should read first. It may read anything, but this is the context it needs.
- Body sections: **Intent** (why), **Deliverable** (what exists when done), **Acceptance** (commands that must pass), **Out of scope**, **Report back**.

Keep each one finishable in a single session with a diff that someone can review in one sitting. When a workorder grows past that, split it.

## Orchestrating

Before handing anything out, check the queue. Every line must be `"verdict":"valid"`:

```bash
mise exec -- argc --argc-run usage bash src/core/contract/usage.sh check .skogai/workorders/open/*.md
```

Hand a workorder to an agent with this prompt, filling in `<name>`:

> Implement the workorder `.skogai/workorders/open/<name>.md` in skogai-runner. Read it and its `reads` first, along with `CLAUDE.md`. Create or change only the paths listed under `owns`. If the work needs anything else, stop and say so instead of widening the change. Run every Acceptance command. Commit on a branch named `wo/<name>`, open a draft PR titled `wo/<name>: <description>`, and reply with what changed, the acceptance output, and anything left undone.

Review the PR against Acceptance and check that the diff touches nothing outside `owns`. Then merge it and move the file to `done/`. The lead updates the bookkeeping: `.harness/*`, `docs/plan.md` status, and this file.

## Open decisions

These came up while writing this queue. They are recorded here, not settled.

- **Path base.** The checker resolves `owns` relative to the declaring file's own directory, and rejects `..` and absolute paths. Workorders mean repo-root-relative paths. Conflict detection is still correct because every open workorder sits in the same folder. The `path-outside-scope` rule does not mark the repo boundary for these files.
- **`depends_on` after completion.** A dependency that moves to `done/` drops out of a check over `open/` and shows up as `missing-dependency`. Checking `done/` as well would make finished workorders' `owns` conflict with new ones. Until this is decided, open workorders are independent and don't use `depends_on`.
- **Directory overlap.** `ownership-conflict` compares normalized paths for equality and doesn't detect a parent directory and its child. Workorders own files only until the checker covers that case or it is decided that it shouldn't.
- **Enforcement.** `owns` is declared, not enforced. `src/core/run/argc.sh run` enforces it for a module's command, but not for agents working these workorders; review is the guard here.

## Domain: core runner

### Decisions
- bash + argc chosen: argc gives one declarative CLI surface (help, completion, parsing) usable by humans and agents alike (2026-10-29)
- `best-version-so-far/` contains active module plans and reusable implementation. Foundation work comes first; tasks may reuse it deliberately. `agents/` and `docs/argc*` also contain reference material. Earlier validation claims need rechecking (clarified 2026-10-29)

- F001 is the relationship contract checker only (spec-gated 2026-10-30). Invalid input is a verdict (JSONL on stdout, exit 0); exit 2 bad args, exit 1 missing yq/jq. Old proposals (split main.sh, .skogai override, single binary) deferred per docs/plan.md (2026-10-30)
- Open plan-step-1 items, not yet features: operation identity / retry / linked intent revisions; configuration ownership and precedence (mise vs git config vs env vs module defaults). Step 2 writable-scope enforcement decided by skogix (2026-11-06): Podman, staged output. The command runs in Podman with the repo mounted read-only (as `mise run test:container` does) plus one empty writable output dir; the runner then verifies the output dir holds only paths in `owns` and only then moves them into place atomically. Out-of-scope writes are impossible inside the container (ro mount) and out-of-scope outputs are rejected before any effect. Implemented as F002 (2026-11-06): src/core/run/argc.sh check|run, example examples/hello.
- usage twins (2026-11-06): to compare argc with usage + mise, every argc piece has a usage twin with the same behavior and tests: `contract/usage.sh`, `run/usage.sh` (+ `examples/usage/hello`, `tests/fixtures/run-usage`), and `main-usage.sh` (`skogai`: no template/sync, usage `mount` reads the registry live; `SKOGAI_COMMANDS` is a `:`-list of registry layers, nearest first). Not spec-gated features; no entry in features.json. Until the comparison is decided, a change to a rule, runner, example or fixture goes into both twins. Open for skogix: criteria and decision for argc vs usage, and whether packaging (PKGBUILD) ships `skogai`.

- usage + mise chosen over argc as the interface for user, agents and modules (skogix, 2026-11-06). New work goes into the usage files only; the argc files are frozen, not removed. Why: one interface instead of twinning every change; usage gives layered registries (`SKOGAI_COMMANDS`), `effect=` for agents via `usage mcp`, and mise integration.
- Module model and config answers (skogix, 2026-11-07). `best-version-so-far/` is the reference target (config fold, module env, install by copy); it is deleted once everything is converted.
  - A module is three things: key/value config defaults, a usage declaration (strictly typed input -> output), and relationships. Candidate shape: one mise file, e.g. `mise.<name>.toml` (format not settled).
  - Relationships: `owns` = creates and is responsible for; `writes` = edits, i.e. gives input to the owning module to react to or use; `watches` = on an event at x, hand the event to executable y.
  - The entrypoint runs a module from anywhere (e.g. local). Once its tests and rules pass, it is copied to global (`~/.config/skogai`) or system (`/etc/skogai`).
  - Precedence, later wins: module defaults, system, global, local, override, command parameters, env. Plain Unix CLI practice.
  - Types are deferred; later modules validate paths, ints and so on.
  - Key/env names: kebab-case. `-` is part of a word and dropped in env; `.` maps to `_`, so `a.b-c.d` = `SKOGAI_A_BC_D` and `SKOGAI_FOO_BAR` = `skogai.foo.bar`.
  - Each module defines its own env, injected when it runs (mise does this for tasks).
  - `depends_on` at run time = the called command is available, i.e. that module is installed.
  - Workorder paths are relative to the git root.
- Verified in mise 2026.10.17 (scratch, 2026-11-07): a task's `usage` field validates args (a missing `<who>` is refused); `MISE_ENV=<name>` loads `mise.<name>.toml`; `[_.skogai]` free-form keys are readable with `mise config get`; `mise.local.toml` overrides it. A plain `[env]` value beats the caller's env. `"{{ get_env(name='X', default='d') }}"` lets the caller's env win, which the precedence above needs.
- mise conf.d (verified 2026-11-07, scratch): mise loads every `conf.d/*.toml` at each level: `/etc/mise/conf.d` (system; this host already has omarchy files there), `~/.config/mise/conf.d` (global, follows `MISE_CONFIG_DIR`), and the project's `.config/mise/conf.d` or `.mise/conf.d`. Tasks in a conf.d file run. `MISE_OVERRIDE_CONFIG_FILENAMES=skogai.toml` also works but is not needed. Layer merge (same session): `[env]` merges key by key and the later layer wins; a later `[tasks.x]` replaces the whole task, so `run` and `usage` vanish silently; `mise config get _.x` reads only the nearest file. An empty .toml parses to `null` in yq. A test can isolate mise with `env -i` plus MISE_CONFIG_DIR, MISE_SYSTEM_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR, MISE_STATE_DIR, MISE_CACHE_DIR and MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS: then `/etc/mise/conf.d` is not loaded. Proposal under discussion: a module's toml is a conf.d drop-in, and installing a module = copying it into the conf.d of the chosen level. Module entry docs (skogix): `SKOGAI.md` rather than AGENTS/CLAUDE/GEMINI/CODEX.md, plus MODULE.md or README.md for the module (not settled). `watches` is deferred.
- Config layering on mise (verified 2026-11-07, scratch, mise 2026.10.17; basis of F004/F005): skogix's precedence maps onto mise as module default `K = "{{ env.K | default(value='d') }}"` in a conf.d (env.K sees the caller env and earlier layers, so a project-installed module still loses to system/global) < `$MISE_SYSTEM_DIR/config.toml` < `$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml` < `<git root>/mise.toml` < `mise.local.toml` (< `config.override.toml`, which `mise set --override` writes). Stored values written as `{{ get_env(name='K', default='v') }}` let the caller env win at every layer, inside tasks too; a plain value beats the caller env. `mise env --json` gives the resolved values. `mise set` (list) names the module file as source even when another layer supplied the value, so origin must be computed by skogai. Within one level conf.d files load before config.toml.
- Evidence starts from the skogai-core hook log shape (`/home/skogix/skogai/.skogai/logs/skogai-core/log.jsonl`: `{ts, event, action?, input}`), extended with run identity and outcome, not a new format (2026-11-06).

### Patterns
- Tests isolate HOME under `$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR` and drive the template via `argc --argc-run`.

### Gotchas
- Rootless podman finds its images through XDG_DATA_HOME (default $HOME/.local/share). Tests that isolate HOME must capture and export XDG_DATA_HOME first, or `podman image exists` fails. This host exports XDG_DATA_HOME already, which hides the problem.
- Do not add `:Z` to podman mounts of module dirs: SELinux relabelling changes the host directory, which is an effect outside `owns`.
- The runner logs to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/skogai/run.jsonl`. This host exports XDG_STATE_HOME, so isolating HOME alone leaks test runs into the real log: tests must set XDG_STATE_HOME and unset SKOGAI_LOG.
- A script reached through a registry symlink must `realpath` `BASH_SOURCE` before locating siblings (fixed in run/usage.sh, 9e82212). The tests copy `examples/usage/hello` whole, so a gitignored `greeting.txt` from a real run breaks 8 tests.
- Never write a file from `jq ... > file` in the Bash tool: a hook rewrites `jq` (even `/usr/bin/jq`) to `rtk jq`, which shortens long strings with `...`. This corrupted features.json once (2026-11-07, restored from git). Put the jq call in a script file and run `bash script.sh`.
- Workorder agents in worktrees under ~/skogai-runner/.claude/worktrees: a hook refuses plain `git` (rtk wrapper); they used `/usr/bin/git`. `mise tasks` there also picks up the parent checkout's mise.toml.
- `mise run test` stays on argc for the twinned files; `mise run test:usage` runs contract.bats and run.bats with `CONTRACT_IMPL=usage RUN_IMPL=usage` plus main-usage.bats. Both suites must pass after a twinned change.
- `contract/usage.sh` receives the variadic `file` as one shell-quoted string (`eval "files=(...)"`); under a usage mount, `usage_cmd` is the mounted script's `bin`, so main-usage.sh dispatches on argv.
- `mise run test` now depends on `mise run image` (cached `podman build`, a no-op without podman).
- No coverage tooling for bash/bats yet: the 95% coverage gate cannot be measured. `full_test` runs `bats tests` only. Enabling coverage (e.g. bashcov/kcov) needs its own feature if wanted.
- `ssh -T git@github.com` fails (no key loaded); remote is HTTPS under `skogai2`. The identity hook checks name/email only.
